c-max-element.title: Find the Largest Number
description: Given a non-empty array of integers nums, return the largest value in it.
Do it in a single pass without sorting.
c-max-element.hint: Keep the best value seen so far and compare every element with it.

c-second-largest.title: Second Largest Distinct Number
description: Given an array of integers nums, return the second largest distinct value. If every value is the same, return -1.
c-second-largest.hint: Track two variables, largest and second, updating them as you scan once.

c-missing-number.title: Missing Number
description: An array nums holds n distinct numbers taken from the range 0 to n. Exactly one number in that range is missing. Return it.
c-missing-number.hint: The sum of 0..n is n(n+1)/2. Subtract what you have.

c-max-consecutive-ones.title: Max Consecutive Ones
description: Given a binary array nums (only 0s and 1s), return the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s.
c-max-consecutive-ones.hint: Count the current run; reset it to 0 on every 0 and remember the best.

c-majority-element.title: Majority Element
description: Given an array nums of size n, return the element that appears more than n / 2 times. Such an element always exists.
c-majority-element.hint: Boyer-Moore voting: keep a candidate and a count; same value adds 1, different value subtracts 1.

c-rotate-array.title: Rotate Array
description: Given an integer array nums, rotate it to the right by k steps and return the rotated array.
c-rotate-array.hint: k can be larger than the length: use k % n. Reversing the whole array, then both parts, rotates in place.

c-product-except-self.title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer where answer[i] is the product of all elements of nums except nums[i].
Solve it without using division, in O(n) time.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 32-bit integer
c-product-except-self.hint: answer[i] = (product of everything left of i) x (product of everything right of i). Build both in two passes.

c-count-vowels.title: Count the Vowels
description: Given a string s, return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u, in either case) it contains.
c-count-vowels.hint: Loop over the characters and check membership in "aeiouAEIOU".

c-valid-palindrome.title: Valid Palindrome
description: A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all letters to lowercase and removing every character that isn't a letter or digit, it reads the same forward and backward.
Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome.
c-valid-palindrome.hint: Two pointers from both ends; skip characters that aren't letters or digits.

input.s: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

c-longest-common-prefix.title: Longest Common Prefix
description: Return the longest string that is a prefix of every string in the array strs. If there is none, return an empty string.
c-longest-common-prefix.hint: Compare character by character with the first string until any string differs or ends.

c-first-unique-char.title: First Unique Character
description: Given a string s of lowercase letters, return the index of the first character that appears exactly once. If there isn't one, return -1.
c-first-unique-char.hint: Count every character first (an int[26] works), then scan again for the first count of 1.

c-reverse-words.title: Reverse Words in a String
description: Given a string s, reverse the order of its words. Words are separated by spaces; the result must have single spaces between words and no leading or trailing spaces.
c-reverse-words.hint: Split on runs of spaces, then join the words in reverse order.

c-string-compression.title: String Compression
description: Compress a string by replacing each run of the same character with the character followed by the run length, but only if that makes it shorter. Example: "aabcccccaaa" becomes "a2b1c5a3".
If the compressed string is not shorter than the original, return the original.
c-string-compression.hint: Walk the string counting each run; build the result with a StringBuilder.

c-contains-duplicate.title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.
c-contains-duplicate.hint: Add each value to a hash set; if it is already there, you found a duplicate.

c-valid-anagram.title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s: the same letters with the same counts, in any order.
c-valid-anagram.hint: Count letters of s up and letters of t down in one int[26]; all zeros means anagram.

c-two-sum-count.title: Count Pairs With a Given Sum
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return how many index pairs (i, j) with i < j satisfy nums[i] + nums[j] == k.
c-two-sum-count.hint: Scan left to right; for each x, add how many times k - x was seen before, then record x in a map.

c-longest-consecutive.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers (like 1, 2, 3, 4) that can be formed from its values.
Aim for O(n) time.
c-longest-consecutive.hint: Put everything in a set. Only start counting from x when x - 1 is not in the set.

c-group-anagrams-count.title: Count Anagram Groups
description: Given an array of strings strs, group words that are anagrams of each other and return how many groups there are.
c-group-anagrams-count.hint: Use the sorted letters of each word as a key in a map (or set).

c-move-zeroes.title: Move Zeroes
description: Given an integer array nums, move all 0s to the end while keeping the relative order of the other elements. Return the array.
c-move-zeroes.hint: Keep a write pointer: copy each non-zero forward, then fill the rest with zeros.

c-squares-sorted.title: Squares of a Sorted Array
description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number, also sorted in non-decreasing order.
Try for O(n) instead of squaring and sorting.
c-squares-sorted.hint: The largest square is at one of the two ends. Fill the answer from the back with two pointers.

c-two-sum-sorted.title: Two Sum II (Sorted Input)
description: Given a 1-indexed array numbers sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers that add up to target and return their indices [index1, index2] with index1 < index2.
There is exactly one solution. Use only constant extra space.
c-two-sum-sorted.hint: Start pointers at both ends: if the sum is too small move left up, if too big move right down.

c-container-most-water.title: Container With Most Water
description: height[i] is the height of a vertical line at position i. Pick two lines that, with the x-axis, hold the most water. Return that maximum amount.
The water held between lines i and j is (j - i) x min(height[i], height[j]).
c-container-most-water.hint: Start with the widest pair and always move the shorter line inward: the taller one can't do better by moving.

c-max-sum-k.title: Maximum Sum of k Consecutive Elements
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the largest sum of any k consecutive elements.
c-max-sum-k.hint: Sum the first k elements, then slide: add the new element, subtract the one that left.

c-min-size-subarray.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
description: Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer target, return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target. Return 0 if there is none.
c-min-size-subarray.hint: Grow the window to the right; while its sum is big enough, record the length and shrink from the left.

c-longest-substring-k-distinct.title: Longest Substring With At Most Two Distinct Letters
description: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains at most two distinct characters.
c-longest-substring-k-distinct.hint: Keep counts of the letters in the window; when there are 3 distinct, shrink from the left until there are 2.

c-running-sum.title: Running Sum of an Array
description: Given an array nums, return its running sum: result[i] = nums[0] + nums[1] + ... + nums[i].
c-running-sum.hint: Each answer is the previous answer plus the current element.

c-pivot-index.title: Find Pivot Index
description: Return the leftmost index where the sum of all numbers to its left equals the sum of all numbers to its right. If no such index exists, return -1.
c-pivot-index.hint: With the total sum known, right = total - left - nums[i]. One pass.

c-subarray-sum-k.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
c-subarray-sum-k.hint: A subarray (i, j] sums to k when prefix[j] - prefix[i] == k. Count earlier prefixes in a map.

c-merge-sorted-arrays.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two arrays a and b, each sorted in non-decreasing order, return one sorted array containing all their elements.
c-merge-sorted-arrays.hint: Two pointers: take the smaller head each time, then copy whatever is left.

c-sort-colors.title: Sort Colors
description: nums contains only 0s, 1s and 2s (red, white, blue). Sort it so all 0s come first, then 1s, then 2s, without using a library sort. Return the array.
A one-pass solution exists (the Dutch national flag algorithm).
c-sort-colors.hint: Keep three regions with pointers low, mid, high and swap 0s left, 2s right.

c-merge-intervals.title: Merge Intervals
description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the result sorted by start.
Intervals that touch, like [1,4] and [4,5], also merge.
c-merge-intervals.hint: Sort by start. Then each interval either extends the last merged one or starts a new one.

c-sort-array.title: Sort an Array (Merge Sort)
description: Sort the integer array nums in ascending order and return it, without using any built-in sort. Aim for O(n log n): implement merge sort or quick sort yourself.
c-sort-array.hint: Merge sort: sort each half recursively, then merge the two sorted halves.

c-search-insert.title: Search Insert Position
description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers nums and a target, return the index of target if it is present, or the index where it would be inserted to keep the order. Use O(log n) time.
c-search-insert.hint: Find the first index whose value is >= target. When the loop ends, low is the answer.

c-first-last-position.title: First and Last Position of a Value
description: Given a sorted array nums and a target, return [first, last]: the first and last index where target appears, or [-1, -1] if it doesn't. Use O(log n) time.
c-first-last-position.hint: Run binary search twice: once biased left to find the first, once biased right to find the last.

c-min-rotated.title: Minimum in a Rotated Sorted Array
description: A sorted array of distinct values was rotated at an unknown pivot, e.g. [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] became [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]. Return its smallest element in O(log n) time.
c-min-rotated.hint: Compare mid with the right end: if nums[mid] > nums[right], the minimum is to the right of mid.

c-koko-bananas.title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: piles[i] is a pile of bananas. Koko eats at speed k bananas per hour: each hour she picks one pile and eats k from it (or the whole pile if it has fewer). She has h hours.
Return the smallest integer speed k that lets her finish every pile within h hours.
c-koko-bananas.hint: Binary search on the answer: for a speed k, the hours needed are the sum of ceil(pile / k).

c-factorial.title: Factorial
description: Return n! (n factorial), the product 1 x 2 x ... x n. By definition 0! = 1. Write it recursively.
c-factorial.hint: Base case: n <= 1 returns 1. Otherwise n x factorial(n - 1).

c-fibonacci.title: Fibonacci Number
description: The Fibonacci numbers start F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, and F(n) = F(n - 1) + F(n - 2). Given n, return F(n).
c-fibonacci.hint: Plain recursion recomputes the same values. Remember results (memoisation) or loop with two variables.

c-power-of-two.title: Power of Two
description: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...).
c-power-of-two.hint: Recursively: n is a power of two if n == 1, or n is even and n / 2 is a power of two.

c-sum-digits.title: Sum of Digits
description: Given a non-negative integer n, return the sum of its decimal digits, using recursion.
c-sum-digits.hint: sumDigits(n) = n % 10 + sumDigits(n / 10), with 0 as the base case.

c-pow-x-n.title: Pow(x, n)
description: Implement pow(x, n): x raised to the integer power n (n may be negative). Use fast exponentiation, O(log n).
c-pow-x-n.hint: x^n = (x^(n/2))^2, times x when n is odd. For negative n, compute 1 / x^(-n).

c-remove-adjacent-duplicates.title: Remove Adjacent Duplicates
description: Repeatedly remove two adjacent equal letters from s until no such pair remains. Return the final string.
c-remove-adjacent-duplicates.hint: Use a stack: push each letter, but pop instead when it equals the top.

c-baseball-game.title: Baseball Game Scores
description: You record scores from operations: an integer x adds a new score x; "+" adds the sum of the previous two scores; "D" adds double the previous score; "C" removes the previous score.
Return the sum of all scores after every operation.
c-baseball-game.hint: A stack of scores makes each operation a push or a pop.

c-next-greater.title: Next Greater Element
description: For each element of nums, find the first element to its right that is strictly greater. Return those values, using -1 where there is none.
c-next-greater.hint: Scan from the right with a stack of candidates; pop everything not greater than the current value.

c-daily-temperatures.title: Daily Temperatures
description: Given daily temperatures, return an array where answer[i] is how many days after day i you wait for a warmer temperature, or 0 if it never comes.
c-daily-temperatures.hint: Keep a stack of indices still waiting for a warmer day; resolve them when a warmer one arrives.

c-eval-rpn.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
description: Evaluate an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation, given as tokens. Operators are +, -, *, /. Division truncates toward zero. Return the result.
c-eval-rpn.hint: Push numbers; on an operator pop two (the second popped is the left operand), apply it, push the result.

c-reverse-linked-list.title: Reverse Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.
ListNode has fields val and next.
c-reverse-linked-list.hint: Walk the list keeping prev, curr and next; point curr.next back to prev at each step.

c-middle-linked-list.title: Middle of the Linked List
description: Return the middle node of a linked list. If there are two middle nodes, return the second one. (The returned list runs from that node to the end.)
c-middle-linked-list.hint: Slow pointer moves 1 step, fast moves 2; when fast reaches the end, slow is in the middle.

c-remove-duplicates-list.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
description: Given the head of a sorted linked list, delete duplicates so each value appears once. Return the list.
c-remove-duplicates-list.hint: If curr.next has the same value as curr, skip it with curr.next = curr.next.next.

c-merge-lists-palindrome.title: Palindrome Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, return true if its values read the same forward and backward.
c-merge-lists-palindrome.hint: Find the middle, reverse the second half, then compare the halves node by node.

c-remove-nth-from-end.title: Remove Nth Node From End
description: Remove the n-th node from the end of a linked list and return its head.
c-remove-nth-from-end.hint: Move a fast pointer n steps ahead, then move both; a dummy node before head handles removing the head.

c-odd-even-list.title: Odd Even Linked List
description: Reorder a linked list so all nodes at odd positions (1st, 3rd, ...) come first, followed by nodes at even positions, keeping the relative order within each group.
c-odd-even-list.hint: Build two chains, odd and even, as you walk; then attach even's head to odd's tail.

c-diagonal-sum.title: Matrix Diagonal Sum
description: Given a square matrix mat, return the sum of its primary diagonal and secondary diagonal, counting the centre element only once when n is odd.
c-diagonal-sum.hint: Add mat[i][i] and mat[i][n-1-i] for each row; subtract the centre once if n is odd.

c-rotate-image.title: Rotate Image
description: Rotate an n x n matrix 90 degrees clockwise and return it. Try to do it in place.
c-rotate-image.hint: Transpose the matrix, then reverse each row.

c-set-matrix-zeroes.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
description: If an element of the matrix is 0, set its entire row and column to 0. Return the matrix.
c-set-matrix-zeroes.hint: First record which rows and columns contain a zero, then zero them in a second pass.

c-spiral-order.title: Spiral Order
description: Return all elements of an m x n matrix in spiral order: along the top row, down the right column, back along the bottom, up the left, and inward.
c-spiral-order.hint: Keep four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) and shrink them after walking each side.

c-count-set-bits.title: Number of 1 Bits
description: Given a non-negative integer n, return how many 1 bits its binary representation has.
c-count-set-bits.hint: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit; count how many times you can do it.

c-single-number.title: Single Number
description: Every element in nums appears twice except one. Return that one, using O(1) extra space.
c-single-number.hint: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR of everything leaves the single number.

c-counting-bits.title: Counting Bits
description: Given n, return an array ans of length n + 1 where ans[i] is the number of 1 bits in i.

c-assign-cookies.title: Assign Cookies
description: Child i is content with a cookie of size at least g[i]; cookie j has size s[j]. Each child gets at most one cookie. Return the maximum number of content children.
c-assign-cookies.hint: Sort both. Give each cookie, smallest first, to the least greedy child it can satisfy.

c-stock-ii.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
description: prices[i] is a stock's price on day i. You may buy and sell many times, holding at most one share at a time. Return the maximum profit.

c-jump-game.title: Jump Game
description: You start at index 0 of nums; nums[i] is the maximum jump length from i. Return true if you can reach the last index.
c-jump-game.hint: Track the furthest index reachable so far; if you ever stand beyond it, you're stuck.

c-max-depth-tree.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Return the maximum depth of a binary tree: the number of nodes on the longest path from the root down to a leaf.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-max-depth-tree.hint: depth(node) = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)); an empty tree has depth 0.

c-invert-tree.title: Invert Binary Tree
description: Mirror a binary tree (swap every node's left and right children) and return its root.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-invert-tree.hint: Swap the children of the root, then invert both subtrees recursively.

c-same-tree.title: Same Tree
description: Given the roots of two binary trees p and q, return true if they have the same shape and the same values.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-same-tree.hint: Both empty: true. One empty or values differ: false. Otherwise compare left and right recursively.

c-inorder-traversal.title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
description: Return the values of a binary tree in inorder: left subtree, then the node, then right subtree.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-inorder-traversal.hint: Recursion is three lines. For an iterative version, push left children onto a stack.

c-path-sum.title: Path Sum
description: Return true if the tree has a root-to-leaf path whose values add up to targetSum.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-path-sum.hint: Subtract each node's value as you go down; at a leaf, check whether what's left equals its value.

c-level-order.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Return the values of a binary tree level by level, left to right: one list per level.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-level-order.hint: Use a queue. Each round, process exactly as many nodes as the queue held at the start: that's one level.

c-validate-bst.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Return true if the tree is a valid binary search tree: every node's left subtree holds only smaller values and its right subtree only larger values.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-validate-bst.hint: Pass down the allowed (low, high) range, or check that an inorder traversal is strictly increasing.

c-diameter-tree.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
description: Return the diameter of a binary tree: the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes. The path may skip the root.
The tree is given in level order, with null for a missing child (as on LeetCode). TreeNode has fields val, left and right.
c-diameter-tree.hint: At each node the longest path through it is height(left) + height(right). Track the best while computing heights.

c-last-stone.title: Last Stone Weight
description: Each turn, smash the two heaviest stones x <= y together: if equal both vanish, otherwise a stone of weight y - x remains. Return the weight of the last stone, or 0 if none are left.
c-last-stone.hint: A max-heap gives you the two heaviest stones each turn.

c-kth-largest.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description: Return the k-th largest element of nums (in sorted order, not the k-th distinct). Try a min-heap of size k instead of sorting everything.
c-kth-largest.hint: Keep a min-heap of the k largest seen; its top is the answer.

c-top-k-frequent.title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Return the k most frequent elements of nums, ordered from most to least frequent. Break ties by the smaller value first.
c-top-k-frequent.hint: Count with a map, then pick the top k by (count desc, value asc) with a heap or a sort.

c-k-closest.title: K Closest Points to Origin
description: Given points [x, y], return the k points closest to the origin (0, 0), nearest first. Break ties by smaller x, then smaller y.
c-k-closest.hint: Compare squared distances (no square roots needed). A max-heap of size k keeps the closest.

c-generate-parentheses.title: Generate Parentheses
description: Given n pairs of parentheses, return every well-formed combination, sorted in lexicographic order ("(" comes before ")").
c-generate-parentheses.hint: Build the string character by character: add "(" while open < n, add ")" while close < open.

c-subsets.title: Subsets
description: Given an array of distinct integers nums sorted ascending, return all of its subsets. Each subset keeps nums' order, and the list of subsets is in lexicographic order (so [] first, then [1], [1,2], ...).
c-subsets.hint: Depth-first: at each index decide to take nums[i] or skip it. Visiting "take" before moving on gives lexicographic order.

c-permutations.title: Permutations
description: Given an array of distinct integers nums sorted ascending, return all permutations in lexicographic order.
c-permutations.hint: Choose each unused number in increasing order for the next position, recurse, then un-choose it.

c-combination-sum-count.title: Combination Sum (Count)
description: Given distinct positive candidates and a target, count the unique combinations whose values add up to target. A candidate may be used any number of times; [2,2,3] and [3,2,2] are the same combination.
c-combination-sum-count.hint: Recurse with a start index so you never go back to earlier candidates: that's what prevents duplicates.

c-flood-fill.title: Flood Fill
description: image is a grid of colours. Starting at (sr, sc), recolour that pixel and every pixel connected to it (up, down, left, right) with the same original colour to the new colour. Return the image.
c-flood-fill.hint: DFS or BFS from the start; if the new colour equals the old one, return the image unchanged.

c-number-of-islands.title: Number of Islands
description: grid is a map of 1s (land) and 0s (water). An island is land connected up, down, left or right. Return the number of islands.
c-number-of-islands.hint: Scan every cell; each time you find unvisited land, count an island and sink all of it with DFS or BFS.

c-max-area-island.title: Max Area of Island
description: In a grid of 1s (land) and 0s (water), return the area (number of cells) of the largest island, or 0 if there is no land. Cells connect up, down, left and right.
c-max-area-island.hint: Same as counting islands, but have the DFS return how many cells it sank.

c-rotting-oranges.title: Rotting Oranges
description: In the grid, 0 is empty, 1 is a fresh orange and 2 is a rotten one. Every minute, fresh oranges next to a rotten one (up, down, left, right) rot. Return the minutes until none are fresh, or -1 if that never happens.
c-rotting-oranges.hint: Multi-source BFS: start the queue with every rotten orange and count levels.

c-number-of-provinces.title: Number of Provinces
description: isConnected[i][j] is 1 if cities i and j are directly connected. A province is a group of cities connected directly or indirectly. Return the number of provinces.
c-number-of-provinces.hint: Run DFS from every unvisited city; each new start is a new province.

c-course-schedule.title: Course Schedule
description: There are numCourses courses labelled 0 to numCourses - 1. prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means you must take b before a. Return true if you can finish every course (that is, there is no cycle).
c-course-schedule.hint: Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take courses with no remaining prerequisites; if you take all of them, there's no cycle.

c-climbing-stairs.title: Climbing Stairs
description: You climb a staircase of n steps, taking 1 or 2 steps at a time. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?
c-climbing-stairs.hint: ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2). It's Fibonacci in disguise.

c-min-cost-stairs.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
description: cost[i] is the cost of stepping on stair i. You can start at stair 0 or 1, and climb 1 or 2 stairs at a time. Return the minimum cost to reach just past the last stair.
c-min-cost-stairs.hint: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i - 1], dp[i - 2]); the answer is min of the last two.

c-house-robber.title: House Robber
description: nums[i] is the money in house i along a street. You can't rob two adjacent houses. Return the most money you can rob.
c-house-robber.hint: For each house: best = max(skip it, rob it + best from two houses back).

c-coin-change.title: Coin Change
description: Given coin denominations and an amount, return the fewest coins that make up the amount, or -1 if it can't be made. You have unlimited coins of each kind.
c-coin-change.hint: dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a - coin]) over coins that fit; dp[0] = 0.

c-unique-paths.title: Unique Paths
description: A robot at the top-left of an m x n grid can only move right or down. How many different paths reach the bottom-right corner?
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer
c-unique-paths.hint: paths[r][c] = paths[r - 1][c] + paths[r][c - 1]; the first row and column are all 1.

c-lis.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of nums (elements in order, not necessarily adjacent).
c-lis.hint: O(n^2): dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) for j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]. O(n log n) uses binary search on tails.

c-lcs.title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Return the length of the longest subsequence common to strings text1 and text2 (characters in order, not necessarily adjacent).
c-lcs.hint: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if the characters match, else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

c-count-digits.title: Count Digits
description: Given a non-negative integer n, return how many digits it has. 0 has one digit.
c-count-digits.hint: Divide by 10 until the number becomes 0, counting the steps (handle 0 separately).

c-palindrome-number.title: Palindrome Number
description: Return true if the integer x reads the same backward as forward. Negative numbers are never palindromes. Try it without converting to a string.
c-palindrome-number.hint: Build the reversed number digit by digit (rev = rev * 10 + x % 10) and compare.

c-reverse-integer.title: Reverse Integer
description: Reverse the digits of a 32-bit signed integer x. If the reversed value falls outside the 32-bit signed range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1], return 0.
c-reverse-integer.hint: Pop digits with % 10 and push with * 10. Check for overflow before each push.

c-gcd.title: Greatest Common Divisor
description: Return the greatest common divisor of two positive integers a and b.
c-gcd.hint: Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b), and gcd(a, 0) = a.

c-lcm.title: Least Common Multiple
description: Return the least common multiple of two positive integers a and b. The answer fits in a 32-bit integer.
c-lcm.hint: lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b. Divide first to avoid overflow.

c-all-divisors.title: All Divisors
description: Return every positive divisor of n in increasing order. Aim for O(sqrt(n)).
c-all-divisors.hint: Divisors come in pairs (d, n / d) with d <= sqrt(n). Collect both halves, then merge in order.

c-is-prime.title: Check Prime
description: Return true if n is a prime number. 0 and 1 are not prime.
c-is-prime.hint: Only test divisors up to sqrt(n).

c-fizz-buzz.title: Fizz Buzz
description: Return an array of strings for 1..n: "FizzBuzz" for multiples of 15, "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5, otherwise the number itself.
c-fizz-buzz.hint: Check divisibility by 15 first, then 3, then 5.

c-sum-1-to-n.title: Sum of First N Numbers
description: Return 1 + 2 + ... + n. Try both a loop and the closed formula.

c-count-primes.title: Count Primes
description: Return how many prime numbers are strictly less than n. Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes.
c-count-primes.hint: Mark multiples of each prime p starting from p * p as composite.

c-power-of-three.title: Power of Three
description: Return true if n is a power of three (1, 3, 9, 27, ...).
c-power-of-three.hint: Keep dividing by 3 while divisible; you should end at 1.

c-ugly-number.title: Ugly Number
description: An ugly number is a positive integer whose only prime factors are 2, 3 and 5. Return true if n is ugly. 1 counts as ugly.
c-ugly-number.hint: Divide out every 2, 3 and 5; ugly numbers end at 1.

c-add-digits.title: Add Digits
description: Repeatedly add all digits of num until one digit remains, and return it.
c-add-digits.hint: Loop until it's one digit, or use the digital-root formula 1 + (num - 1) % 9.

c-happy-number.title: Happy Number
description: Replace n by the sum of the squares of its digits, repeatedly. If this reaches 1, n is happy; if it loops forever without reaching 1, it isn't. Return whether n is happy.
c-happy-number.hint: Detect the cycle with a set of seen values, or with slow and fast pointers.

c-valid-perfect-square.title: Valid Perfect Square
description: Return true if num is a perfect square, without using a built-in square root.
c-valid-perfect-square.hint: Binary search k in [1, num] for k * k == num (use long for the product).

c-excel-column-number.title: Excel Column Number
description: Excel columns are labelled A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ... Given a column title, return its column number (A = 1, Z = 26, AA = 27).
c-excel-column-number.hint: It's base 26 with digits 1..26: result = result * 26 + (ch - 'A' + 1).

c-excel-column-title.title: Excel Column Title
description: Given a column number, return its Excel column title (1 = A, 28 = AB, 701 = ZY).
c-excel-column-title.hint: Subtract 1 before each % 26 step, because there's no zero digit.

c-factorial-trailing-zeroes.title: Factorial Trailing Zeroes
description: Return how many trailing zeros n! has. Do it in O(log n) without computing n!.
c-factorial-trailing-zeroes.hint: Each zero comes from a factor 10 = 2 x 5, and 5s are rarer. Count n/5 + n/25 + n/125 + ...

c-self-dividing-numbers.title: Self Dividing Numbers
description: A self-dividing number is divisible by every one of its digits and contains no 0. Return all self-dividing numbers in [left, right].
c-self-dividing-numbers.hint: For each number, peel off digits with % 10 and test them.

c-tribonacci.title: N-th Tribonacci Number
description: T0 = 0, T1 = 1, T2 = 1 and T(n+3) = T(n) + T(n+1) + T(n+2). Return T(n).
c-tribonacci.hint: Keep the last three values in variables and roll them forward.

c-base-7.title: Base 7
description: Return the base-7 representation of the integer num as a string (negative numbers keep a leading minus).
c-base-7.hint: Repeatedly take num % 7 and divide by 7; the digits come out in reverse.

c-check-sorted.title: Check if Array Is Sorted
description: Return true if nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.
c-check-sorted.hint: Compare each element with the one before it.

c-linear-search.title: Linear Search
description: Return the index of the first occurrence of target in nums, or -1 if it isn't there.
c-linear-search.hint: Scan from the left and stop at the first match.

c-left-rotate-one.title: Left Rotate by One
description: Move every element one place to the left; the first element goes to the end. Return the array.
c-left-rotate-one.hint: Save nums[0], shift the rest left, put the saved value last.

c-union-sorted.title: Union of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays, return their union: every distinct value from either array, in increasing order.
c-union-sorted.hint: Two pointers like merge, skipping a value equal to the last one written.

c-intersection-sorted.title: Intersection of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Given two sorted arrays, return the distinct values that appear in both, in increasing order.
c-intersection-sorted.hint: Advance the pointer at the smaller value; on a match, record it once and advance both.

c-rearrange-by-sign.title: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
description: nums has an equal number of positive and negative integers. Return an arrangement that alternates positive, negative, positive, ... starting with a positive, keeping the original order within each sign.
c-rearrange-by-sign.hint: Write positives to even indices and negatives to odd indices of a result array.

c-next-permutation.title: Next Permutation
description: Rearrange nums into the next lexicographically greater permutation and return it. If it's the largest permutation, return the smallest one (sorted ascending).
c-next-permutation.hint: From the right, find the first i with nums[i] < nums[i+1]; swap it with the smallest larger value to its right; reverse the suffix.

c-leaders.title: Leaders in an Array
description: An element is a leader if it is strictly greater than every element to its right. The last element is always a leader. Return all leaders in their original order.
c-leaders.hint: Scan from the right keeping the maximum seen; collect values above it, then reverse.

c-majority-element-ii.title: Majority Element II
description: Return every value that appears more than n / 3 times in nums, in increasing order.
c-majority-element-ii.hint: At most two such values exist: extended Boyer-Moore with two candidates.

c-four-sum.title: 4Sum
description: Return all unique quadruplets [a, b, c, d] of values from nums (distinct indices) that add up to target. Each quadruplet is sorted ascending, and the list is in lexicographic order.
c-four-sum.hint: Sort, fix two indices with loops, then two pointers for the rest; skip duplicates at every level.

c-maximum-product-subarray.title: Maximum Product Subarray
description: Return the largest product of any contiguous non-empty subarray of nums.
c-maximum-product-subarray.hint: Track both the max and the min product ending here: a negative number swaps them.

c-repeating-and-missing.title: Find the Repeating and Missing Number
description: nums has n numbers from 1..n where exactly one value appears twice and one value is missing. Return [repeating, missing].
c-repeating-and-missing.hint: Use the sum and the sum of squares of 1..n, or a frequency array.

c-count-inversions.title: Count Inversions
description: An inversion is a pair i < j with nums[i] > nums[j]. Return how many inversions nums has. Aim for O(n log n).
c-count-inversions.hint: Merge sort: when you take from the right half, every remaining element on the left forms an inversion.

c-reverse-pairs.title: Reverse Pairs
description: Return how many pairs i < j satisfy nums[i] > 2 * nums[j].
c-reverse-pairs.hint: Merge sort again: before merging two sorted halves, count pairs with a moving pointer. Use long for 2 * nums[j].

c-find-duplicate-number.title: Find the Duplicate Number
description: nums has n + 1 integers in [1, n]; exactly one value repeats (possibly several times). Return it without modifying the array and with O(1) extra space.
c-find-duplicate-number.hint: Treat i -> nums[i] as a linked list; Floyd's cycle detection finds the entrance.

c-third-maximum.title: Third Maximum Number
description: Return the third largest distinct value in nums. If there are fewer than three distinct values, return the largest.
c-third-maximum.hint: Keep three variables for the top three distinct values.

c-plus-one.title: Plus One
description: digits holds a non-negative integer, most significant digit first. Add one and return the resulting digits.
c-plus-one.hint: Walk from the end: a 9 becomes 0 and carries; anything else increments and stops. All 9s grow by a leading 1.

c-find-disappeared-numbers.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
description: nums has n integers, each in [1, n]. Return every value in [1, n] that does not appear, in increasing order.
c-find-disappeared-numbers.hint: Mark presence in place by negating nums[value - 1]; positives left over are the missing ones.

c-array-sign.title: Sign of the Product of an Array
description: Return 1 if the product of all values in nums is positive, -1 if negative, and 0 if it is zero. Don't compute the product.
c-array-sign.hint: Only zeros and the count of negatives matter.

c-check-sorted-rotated.title: Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated
description: Return true if nums could be a non-decreasing array rotated some number of positions (including zero).
c-check-sorted-rotated.hint: Count the places where nums[i] > nums[(i + 1) % n]; at most one is allowed.

c-remove-outermost-parentheses.title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
description: s is a valid parentheses string made of primitive groups like "(()())". Remove the outermost pair of every primitive group and return the result.
c-remove-outermost-parentheses.hint: Track depth: copy a character unless it opens at depth 0 or closes back to depth 0.

c-largest-odd-number.title: Largest Odd Number in String
description: num is a large integer written as a string. Return the largest-valued odd integer that is a non-empty substring of num, or "" if there is none.
c-largest-odd-number.hint: Find the last odd digit; everything up to it is the answer.

c-isomorphic-strings.title: Isomorphic Strings
description: Two strings are isomorphic if the characters of s can be replaced one-to-one to get t (no two characters map to the same one). Return whether s and t are isomorphic.
c-isomorphic-strings.hint: Keep two maps (s->t and t->s) and check both stay consistent.

c-rotate-string.title: Rotate String
description: Return true if goal can be obtained by moving some number of characters from the front of s to its back.
c-rotate-string.hint: Every rotation of s is a substring of s + s.

c-sort-characters-by-frequency.title: Sort Characters by Frequency
description: Sort the characters of s by how often they occur, most frequent first. Characters with equal frequency appear in increasing character order (by code).
c-sort-characters-by-frequency.hint: Count characters, then sort the distinct characters by (count desc, char asc), or bucket by count.

c-max-nesting-depth.title: Maximum Nesting Depth of Parentheses
description: s is a valid expression with digits, operators and parentheses. Return the maximum depth of nested parentheses.
c-max-nesting-depth.hint: Count +1 for "(" and -1 for ")" and remember the maximum.

c-roman-to-integer.title: Roman to Integer
description: Convert a Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M with subtractive pairs like IV and CM) to an integer.
c-roman-to-integer.hint: Add each value, but subtract it when the next symbol is larger.

c-string-to-integer-atoi.title: String to Integer (atoi)
description: Implement atoi: skip leading spaces, read an optional + or -, then read digits until a non-digit. Clamp the result to the 32-bit signed range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1]. If no digits are read, return 0.
c-string-to-integer-atoi.hint: Handle each phase in order: spaces, sign, digits. Check for overflow before multiplying by 10.

c-longest-palindromic-substring.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Return the longest palindromic substring of s. If several have the same length, return the one that starts first.
c-longest-palindromic-substring.hint: Expand around every centre (each character and each gap); keep the longest seen.

c-sum-of-beauty.title: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
description: The beauty of a string is (highest character frequency) - (lowest frequency among characters that appear). Return the sum of the beauty of every substring of s.
c-sum-of-beauty.hint: For each start, extend the end one character at a time while updating a count[26].

c-reverse-vowels.title: Reverse Vowels of a String
description: Reverse only the vowels (a, e, i, o, u in either case) of s and return it.
c-reverse-vowels.hint: Two pointers from both ends that stop on vowels and swap.

c-length-of-last-word.title: Length of Last Word
description: s is words separated by spaces (possibly with trailing spaces). Return the length of the last word.
c-length-of-last-word.hint: Skip trailing spaces from the end, then count letters until the next space.

c-is-subsequence.title: Is Subsequence
description: Return true if s is a subsequence of t: you can delete some characters of t, without reordering, to get s.
c-is-subsequence.hint: Walk t once with a pointer into s that advances on each match.

c-count-palindromic-substrings.title: Palindromic Substrings
description: Return how many substrings of s are palindromes (substrings at different positions count separately).
c-count-palindromic-substrings.hint: Expand around each of the 2n - 1 centres and count every successful expansion.

c-find-first-occurrence.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence
description: Return the index of the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or -1 if needle is not part of haystack.
c-find-first-occurrence.hint: Try each start position and compare; KMP makes it O(n + m).

c-contains-duplicate-ii.title: Contains Duplicate II
description: Return true if there are two different indices i and j with nums[i] == nums[j] and |i - j| <= k.
c-contains-duplicate-ii.hint: Remember the last index of each value in a map.

c-ransom-note.title: Ransom Note
description: Return true if ransomNote can be built from the letters of magazine, using each magazine letter at most once.
c-ransom-note.hint: Count the magazine's letters, then spend them on the note.

c-word-pattern.title: Word Pattern
description: s is words separated by single spaces. Return true if s follows pattern: a one-to-one match between pattern letters and words.
c-word-pattern.hint: Two maps, letter->word and word->letter, must never disagree.

c-jewels-and-stones.title: Jewels and Stones
description: jewels lists the stone types that are jewels; each character of stones is a stone you have. Return how many of your stones are jewels. Letters are case-sensitive.
c-jewels-and-stones.hint: Put jewels in a set and count stones that are in it.

c-intersection-of-arrays-ii.title: Intersection of Two Arrays II
description: Return the intersection of the two arrays where each value appears as many times as it shows in both. Return the values in increasing order.
c-intersection-of-arrays-ii.hint: Count one array, then walk the other decrementing counts.

c-find-the-difference.title: Find the Difference
description: t is s shuffled with one extra letter added. Return that letter as a one-character string.
c-find-the-difference.hint: Count letters, or XOR every character code of both strings.

c-number-of-good-pairs.title: Number of Good Pairs
description: A pair (i, j) is good if nums[i] == nums[j] and i < j. Return the number of good pairs.
c-number-of-good-pairs.hint: Each value seen c times before adds c new pairs when it appears again.

c-unique-occurrences.title: Unique Number of Occurrences
description: Return true if every distinct value in arr occurs a different number of times.
c-unique-occurrences.hint: Count values, then check the counts are distinct with a set.

c-degree-of-array.title: Degree of an Array
description: The degree of an array is the highest frequency of any value. Return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray with the same degree as nums.
c-degree-of-array.hint: For each value record its count, first index and last index.

c-sum-of-unique.title: Sum of Unique Elements
description: Return the sum of the values that appear exactly once in nums.
c-sum-of-unique.hint: Count, then add values whose count is 1.

c-lucky-integer.title: Find Lucky Integer in an Array
description: A lucky integer's frequency equals its value. Return the largest lucky integer, or -1 if there is none.
c-lucky-integer.hint: Count values and keep the best value equal to its count.

c-distribute-candies.title: Distribute Candies
description: Alice has an even number n of candies, candyType[i] being each candy's type. She may eat n / 2 of them. Return the most different types she can eat.
c-distribute-candies.hint: The answer is limited by both the number of types and n / 2.

c-longest-harmonious-subsequence.title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence
description: A harmonious array has max - min exactly 1. Return the length of the longest harmonious subsequence of nums (0 if none).
c-longest-harmonious-subsequence.hint: Count values; for each v with v + 1 present, count[v] + count[v + 1] is a candidate.

c-max-balloons.title: Maximum Number of Balloons
description: Return how many times you can form the word "balloon" using each character of text at most once.
c-max-balloons.hint: Count letters; l and o are needed twice.

c-close-strings.title: Determine if Two Strings Are Close
description: Two strings are close if you can turn one into the other by (1) swapping any two characters, or (2) turning every occurrence of one existing character into another existing character and vice versa. Return whether word1 and word2 are close.
c-close-strings.hint: Same set of letters, and the same multiset of counts.

c-equal-row-column-pairs.title: Equal Row and Column Pairs
description: Return the number of pairs (row i, column j) of the n x n grid where row i and column j contain the same values in the same order.
c-equal-row-column-pairs.hint: Count rows as tuples (or strings) in a map, then look up each column.

c-four-sum-ii.title: 4Sum II
description: Return how many tuples (i, j, k, l) satisfy nums1[i] + nums2[j] + nums3[k] + nums4[l] == 0.
c-four-sum-ii.hint: Store every a + b sum's count in a map, then look up -(c + d).

c-highest-frequency-element.title: Most Frequent Element
description: Return the value that occurs most often in nums. If several tie, return the smallest of them.
c-highest-frequency-element.hint: Count with a map, then pick (highest count, smallest value).

c-count-distinct.title: Count Distinct Elements
description: Return how many distinct values nums contains.
c-count-distinct.hint: Add everything to a hash set and return its size.

c-valid-sudoku.title: Valid Sudoku
description: board has 9 strings of 9 characters: digits 1-9 or '.' for empty. Return true if the filled cells are valid: no repeated digit in any row, column or 3 x 3 box. The board need not be solvable.
c-valid-sudoku.hint: One set per row, column and box; box index = (r / 3) * 3 + c / 3.

c-remove-element.title: Remove Element
description: Remove every occurrence of val from nums in place and return the remaining elements in their original order.
c-remove-element.hint: A write pointer copies each element that isn't val forward.

c-remove-duplicates-ii.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
description: nums is sorted. Remove duplicates in place so each value appears at most twice, and return the result.
c-remove-duplicates-ii.hint: Keep nums[i] when it differs from the element two places back in the written part.

c-three-sum-closest.title: 3Sum Closest
description: Return the sum of three numbers in nums (distinct indices) that is closest to target. Exactly one closest sum exists.
c-three-sum-closest.hint: Sort; fix i and move left/right pointers toward the target, tracking the closest sum.

c-valid-palindrome-ii.title: Valid Palindrome II
description: Return true if s can become a palindrome by deleting at most one character.
c-valid-palindrome-ii.hint: Two pointers; at the first mismatch, try skipping either side once.

c-trapping-rain-water.title: Trapping Rain Water
description: height[i] is the height of a bar of width 1. Return how much rain water is trapped between the bars.
c-trapping-rain-water.hint: Water at i = min(max left, max right) - height[i]. Two pointers move the side with the smaller max.

c-boats-to-save-people.title: Boats to Save People
description: Each boat carries at most two people with total weight at most limit. Return the minimum number of boats to carry everyone (every person weighs at most limit).
c-boats-to-save-people.hint: Sort; pair the heaviest with the lightest whenever they fit.

c-sort-array-by-parity.title: Sort Array by Parity
description: Return nums with all even numbers first and all odd numbers after, keeping the original order within each group.
c-sort-array-by-parity.hint: Two passes with a write pointer, or a result array filled from both groups.

c-reverse-words-iii.title: Reverse Words in a String III
description: s is words separated by single spaces. Reverse the characters of each word while keeping word order.
c-reverse-words-iii.hint: For each word, swap characters from both ends inward.

c-backspace-string-compare.title: Backspace String Compare
description: In s and t, '#' is a backspace. Return true if both strings are equal after applying the backspaces. Try O(1) extra space.
c-backspace-string-compare.hint: Walk both strings from the end, skipping characters that a '#' deletes.

c-min-difference-k-scores.title: Minimum Difference Between Highest and Lowest of K Scores
description: Pick k scores from nums so that the difference between the highest and lowest picked score is as small as possible. Return that difference.
c-min-difference-k-scores.hint: Sort; the best window is k consecutive values.

c-duplicate-zeros.title: Duplicate Zeros
description: Duplicate each zero in arr, shifting the remaining elements right. Elements pushed past the original length are dropped. Return the array (same length).
c-duplicate-zeros.hint: Count how many zeros fit, then fill from the back with two pointers.

c-k-diff-pairs.title: K-diff Pairs in an Array
description: Return the number of unique pairs of values (a, b) in nums with b - a == k (pairs from different indices).
c-k-diff-pairs.hint: Sort and use two pointers, or count values in a map (k == 0 needs a value seen twice).

c-max-k-sum-pairs.title: Max Number of K-Sum Pairs
description: In one operation, remove two numbers that add up to k. Return the maximum number of operations.
c-max-k-sum-pairs.hint: Sort and close in with two pointers, removing a pair when the sum hits k.

c-long-pressed-name.title: Long Pressed Name
description: Some keys may have been held down while typing name, repeating a character. Return true if typed could be name typed with long presses.
c-long-pressed-name.hint: Walk both strings; extra characters in typed must repeat the previous typed character.

c-merge-strings-alternately.title: Merge Strings Alternately
description: Merge two strings by alternating characters, starting with word1. Append the rest of the longer string at the end.
c-merge-strings-alternately.hint: One index into each word; take from each while it has characters.

c-shortest-distance-to-char.title: Shortest Distance to a Character
description: c is a single character that occurs in s. Return an array where answer[i] is the distance from i to the nearest occurrence of c.
c-shortest-distance-to-char.hint: One pass left to right and one right to left, tracking the last position of c.

c-reverse-only-letters.title: Reverse Only Letters
description: Reverse only the English letters of s; every other character stays where it is.
c-reverse-only-letters.hint: Two pointers that skip non-letters and swap letters.

c-partition-around-pivot.title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
description: Rearrange nums so all elements less than pivot come first, then elements equal to pivot, then elements greater, keeping the relative order within each group.
c-partition-around-pivot.hint: Fill less-than from the front and greater-than from the back of a result array.

c-count-pairs-less-than-target.title: Count Pairs Whose Sum Is Less than Target
description: Return how many pairs i < j have nums[i] + nums[j] < target.
c-count-pairs-less-than-target.hint: Sort; if nums[l] + nums[r] < target, all pairs (l, l+1..r) count, so add r - l and move l.

c-two-sum-less-than-k.title: Two Sum Less Than K
description: Return the largest sum nums[i] + nums[j] (i < j) that is strictly less than k, or -1 if none exists.
c-two-sum-less-than-k.hint: Sort, then two pointers: a sum below k is a candidate and moves left up; otherwise move right down.

c-valid-triangle-number.title: Valid Triangle Number
description: Return how many triplets of indices can be the side lengths of a non-degenerate triangle (each pair of sides sums to more than the third).
c-valid-triangle-number.hint: Sort; fix the largest side and count pairs to its left with two pointers.

c-minimize-max-pair-sum.title: Minimize Maximum Pair Sum in Array
description: nums has even length. Split it into pairs so that the largest pair sum is as small as possible. Return that largest pair sum.
c-minimize-max-pair-sum.hint: Sort and pair the smallest with the largest.

c-sum-of-square-numbers.title: Sum of Square Numbers
description: Return true if there are non-negative integers a and b with a^2 + b^2 == c.
c-sum-of-square-numbers.hint: a starts at 0 and b at sqrt(c); move a up when the sum is small and b down when it's large. Use long.

c-interval-list-intersections.title: Interval List Intersections
description: Each list holds sorted, disjoint closed intervals [start, end]. Return their intersection as a sorted list of intervals.
c-interval-list-intersections.hint: Overlap = [max(starts), min(ends)] if non-empty; advance whichever interval ends first.

c-max-average-subarray.title: Maximum Average Subarray I
description: Return the maximum average of any contiguous subarray of length k.
c-max-average-subarray.hint: Slide a window of size k keeping its sum; divide the best sum by k at the end.

c-max-vowels-substring.title: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
description: Return the maximum number of vowels in any substring of s of length k.
c-max-vowels-substring.hint: Add the entering character, subtract the leaving one.

c-character-replacement.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description: You may change at most k characters of s (uppercase letters). Return the length of the longest substring of one repeated letter you can get.
c-character-replacement.hint: Window is valid while length - (count of its most frequent letter) <= k.

c-permutation-in-string.title: Permutation in String
description: Return true if some permutation of s1 is a substring of s2.
c-permutation-in-string.hint: Compare letter counts of a fixed window of size len(s1) as it slides.

c-find-all-anagrams.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
description: Return every start index in s where an anagram of p begins, in increasing order.
c-find-all-anagrams.hint: Same fixed-size window as Permutation in String; record each match.

c-minimum-window-substring.title: Minimum Window Substring
description: Return the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t (with multiplicity). If there are several, return the leftmost; if none, return "".
c-minimum-window-substring.hint: Expand right until the window covers t, then shrink left while it still does, recording the best.

c-sliding-window-maximum.title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: Return the maximum of each window of size k as it slides from left to right.
c-sliding-window-maximum.hint: Keep a deque of indices with decreasing values; the front is the window's max.

c-max-consecutive-ones-iii.title: Max Consecutive Ones III
description: nums is binary. You may flip at most k zeros. Return the longest run of consecutive 1s you can get.
c-max-consecutive-ones-iii.hint: Shrink the window when it holds more than k zeros.

c-fruit-into-baskets.title: Fruit Into Baskets
description: Walking along a row of trees (fruits[i] is the type), you pick one fruit from each tree but your two baskets each hold only one type. Return the most fruit you can pick from one contiguous stretch.
c-fruit-into-baskets.hint: Longest window with at most two distinct values.

c-longest-ones-after-deleting.title: Longest Subarray of 1s After Deleting One Element
description: nums is binary. Delete exactly one element, then return the length of the longest run of 1s.
c-longest-ones-after-deleting.hint: Window with at most one zero; answer is its size minus one.

c-substrings-with-all-three.title: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
description: s contains only a, b and c. Return how many substrings contain at least one of each.
c-substrings-with-all-three.hint: For each right end, count left starts that still include all three: track the last index of each letter.

c-nice-subarrays.title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
description: A subarray is nice if it contains exactly k odd numbers. Return the number of nice subarrays.

c-binary-subarrays-with-sum.title: Binary Subarrays With Sum
description: nums is binary. Return how many non-empty subarrays sum to goal.
c-binary-subarrays-with-sum.hint: atMost(goal) - atMost(goal - 1), or prefix sums with a count map.

c-max-points-from-cards.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
description: Take exactly k cards, each time from the start or the end of the row. Return the maximum total points.
c-max-points-from-cards.hint: Equivalently, find the minimum-sum window of n - k cards left behind.

c-subarrays-k-different.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
description: Return how many subarrays contain exactly k distinct integers.
c-subarrays-k-different.hint: exactly(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1), each a standard sliding window.

c-longest-substring-at-most-k-distinct.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
description: Return the length of the longest substring of s with at most k distinct characters.
c-longest-substring-at-most-k-distinct.hint: Shrink from the left whenever the window has more than k distinct letters.

c-subarrays-avg-threshold.title: Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average at Least Threshold
description: Return how many subarrays of size k have an average greater than or equal to threshold.
c-subarrays-avg-threshold.hint: Compare window sums with k * threshold to avoid division.

c-min-recolors.title: Minimum Recolors to Get K Consecutive Black Blocks
description: blocks has 'W' (white) and 'B' (black). Return the fewest whites you must repaint black to get k consecutive black blocks.
c-min-recolors.hint: Count whites in each window of size k; the minimum is the answer.

c-defuse-the-bomb.title: Defuse the Bomb
description: code is circular. Replace each element: if k > 0, by the sum of the next k elements; if k < 0, by the sum of the previous |k| elements; if k == 0, by 0. Return the new array.
c-defuse-the-bomb.hint: A window of size |k| moving around the circle with modulo indices.

c-distinct-substrings-size-three.title: Substrings of Size Three with Distinct Characters
description: Return how many substrings of length 3 have three different characters (count every occurrence).
c-distinct-substrings-size-three.hint: Check each window of three characters.

c-grumpy-bookstore.title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
description: customers[i] arrive in minute i; if grumpy[i] is 1 they are unsatisfied. Once, the owner can stay calm for `minutes` consecutive minutes. Return the maximum number of satisfied customers.
c-grumpy-bookstore.hint: Base satisfied total plus the best window of grumpy-minute customers you can win back.

c-min-swaps-group-ones.title: Minimum Swaps to Group All 1s Together II
description: nums is a circular binary array. A swap exchanges any two elements. Return the minimum swaps to put all 1s next to each other.
c-min-swaps-group-ones.hint: Window size = number of 1s; the answer is the fewest zeros in any circular window of that size.

c-maximum-erasure-value.title: Maximum Erasure Value
description: Return the maximum sum of a contiguous subarray whose elements are all distinct.
c-maximum-erasure-value.hint: Grow the window; when a value repeats, shrink from the left past its previous copy.

c-frequency-most-frequent.title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
description: In one operation you can increment any element by 1. With at most k operations, return the highest possible frequency of any value.
c-frequency-most-frequent.hint: Sort; a window can all become its max if max * size - sum <= k.

c-min-ops-reduce-x.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
description: Each operation removes the leftmost or rightmost element and subtracts it from x. Return the fewest operations to make x exactly 0, or -1 if impossible.
c-min-ops-reduce-x.hint: Find the longest middle window whose sum is total - x.

c-range-sum-query.title: Range Sum Query
description: Each query [l, r] asks for nums[l] + ... + nums[r]. Return the answers in order. Precompute so each query is O(1).
c-range-sum-query.hint: prefix[i] = sum of the first i values; a range is prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l].

c-range-sum-2d.title: Range Sum Query 2D
description: Each query [r1, c1, r2, c2] asks for the sum of the rectangle with corners (r1, c1) and (r2, c2), inclusive. Return the answers in order.
c-range-sum-2d.hint: Build P[r+1][c+1] = sum of the top-left rectangle; answer by inclusion-exclusion of four corners.

c-contiguous-array.title: Contiguous Array
description: nums is binary. Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s.
c-contiguous-array.hint: Count 0 as -1; a zero-sum subarray sits between two equal prefix sums. Store each prefix's first index.

c-subarray-sums-divisible-by-k.title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
description: Return how many non-empty subarrays have a sum divisible by k.
c-subarray-sums-divisible-by-k.hint: Count prefix sums by their remainder mod k (fix negative remainders); equal remainders pair up.

c-continuous-subarray-sum.title: Continuous Subarray Sum
description: Return true if nums has a subarray of length at least 2 whose sum is a multiple of k.
c-continuous-subarray-sum.hint: Remember the first index of each prefix remainder; a repeat at least 2 apart means yes.

c-highest-altitude.title: Find the Highest Altitude
description: A biker starts at altitude 0; gain[i] is the change between points i and i + 1. Return the highest altitude reached.
c-highest-altitude.hint: Running sum, tracking the maximum (including the start at 0).

c-left-right-sum-differences.title: Left and Right Sum Differences
description: Return answer where answer[i] = |(sum of elements left of i) - (sum of elements right of i)|.
c-left-right-sum-differences.hint: Keep a running left sum; right = total - left - nums[i].

c-min-start-value.title: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum
description: Starting from a positive value, you add nums from left to right. Return the minimum start value so the running total is never below 1.
c-min-start-value.hint: Find the minimum prefix sum m; you need start + m >= 1.

c-ways-to-split-array.title: Number of Ways to Split Array
description: A split at index i (0 <= i < n - 1) is valid if the sum of nums[0..i] is at least the sum of nums[i+1..n-1]. Return the number of valid splits.
c-ways-to-split-array.hint: One running prefix sum compared with total - prefix (use long for big inputs).

c-longest-subarray-sum-k.title: Longest Subarray with Sum K
description: Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray summing to k (values may be negative), or 0 if none.
c-longest-subarray-sum-k.hint: Map each prefix sum to its FIRST index; at j, look for prefix - k.

c-longest-zero-sum-subarray.title: Largest Subarray with 0 Sum
description: Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is 0.
c-longest-zero-sum-subarray.hint: Two equal prefix sums enclose a zero-sum subarray.

c-subarrays-xor-k.title: Count Subarrays with XOR K
description: Return how many subarrays have a bitwise XOR equal to k.
c-subarrays-xor-k.hint: prefixXor[j] ^ prefixXor[i] = xor of the subarray; count earlier prefixes equal to prefixXor[j] ^ k.

c-car-pooling.title: Car Pooling
description: Each trip [passengers, from, to] picks people up at km `from` and drops them at km `to`. The car only drives east. Return true if it never holds more than capacity people.
c-car-pooling.hint: Difference array: +p at from, -p at to; a running sum is the load at each km.

c-corporate-flight-bookings.title: Corporate Flight Bookings
description: Flights are numbered 1..n. Each booking [first, last, seats] reserves seats on every flight from first to last. Return the total seats reserved per flight.
c-corporate-flight-bookings.hint: Add seats at first and subtract after last, then prefix-sum.

c-range-addition.title: Range Addition
description: Start with an array of zeros of the given length. Each update [start, end, inc] adds inc to every index in [start, end]. Return the final array.
c-range-addition.hint: Difference array again: O(1) per update, one prefix pass at the end.

c-shifting-letters.title: Shifting Letters
description: shifts[i] means: shift the first i + 1 letters of s forward by shifts[i] (z wraps to a). Return the final string.
c-shifting-letters.hint: Letter i moves by the suffix sum of shifts from i; compute right to left mod 26.

c-max-score-split-string.title: Maximum Score After Splitting a String
description: Split the binary string s into two non-empty parts. The score is (zeros in the left part) + (ones in the right part). Return the maximum score.
c-max-score-split-string.hint: Count all ones first, then sweep the split point updating both counts.

c-zero-filled-subarrays.title: Number of Zero-Filled Subarrays
description: Return the number of subarrays filled entirely with 0.
c-zero-filled-subarrays.hint: A run of r zeros contributes r(r + 1)/2; equivalently add the current run length at each zero.

c-sum-odd-length-subarrays.title: Sum of All Odd Length Subarrays
description: Return the sum of all elements of every odd-length subarray of arr.
c-sum-odd-length-subarrays.hint: Prefix sums make each subarray O(1); or count how many odd subarrays include each index.

c-minimum-average-difference.title: Minimum Average Difference
description: For index i, the average difference is |floor(avg of first i + 1 elements) - floor(avg of the remaining elements)| (the average of zero elements is 0). Return the index with the smallest difference (the smallest such index on ties).
c-minimum-average-difference.hint: Running prefix sum; suffix = total - prefix. Use long and integer division.

c-vowel-strings-in-ranges.title: Count Vowel Strings in Ranges
description: A word is a vowel string if it starts and ends with a vowel. For each query [l, r], count vowel strings among words[l..r].
c-vowel-strings-in-ranges.hint: Prefix count of vowel strings; each query is a subtraction.

c-ways-to-make-fair-array.title: Ways to Make a Fair Array
description: Removing one index shifts later elements. An array is fair if the sum at even indices equals the sum at odd indices. Return how many indices you could remove to make nums fair.
c-ways-to-make-fair-array.hint: After removing i, elements to its right swap parity. Keep prefix even/odd sums and use totals for the right side.

c-grid-game.title: Grid Game
description: A 2 x n grid. Robot 1 goes from top-left to bottom-right moving right or down once, collecting and zeroing the cells it visits. Then robot 2 does the same, maximising its total. Robot 1 plays to minimise robot 2's total. Return robot 2's total.
c-grid-game.hint: If robot 1 drops down at column i, robot 2 gets max(top suffix after i, bottom prefix before i).

c-plates-between-candles.title: Plates Between Candles
description: s has '*' (plate) and '|' (candle). For each query [l, r], count plates in s[l..r] that have a candle somewhere to their left and right within that substring.
c-plates-between-candles.hint: Prefix count of plates, plus nearest candle to the right of l and to the left of r.

c-range-covered.title: Check if All the Integers in a Range Are Covered
description: Each range [start, end] covers every integer in it. Return true if every integer in [left, right] is covered by at least one range.
c-range-covered.hint: Difference array over the small value range, then check coverage > 0.

c-xor-queries.title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
description: For each query [l, r], return arr[l] XOR arr[l + 1] XOR ... XOR arr[r].

c-prefix-common-array.title: Find the Prefix Common Array of Two Arrays
description: A and B are permutations of 1..n. C[i] is how many numbers appear in both A[0..i] and B[0..i]. Return C.
c-prefix-common-array.hint: Count how many times each number has been seen across both arrays; it's common when its count hits 2.

c-relative-sort-array.title: Relative Sort Array
description: arr2 has distinct values, all present in arr1. Sort arr1 so values appear in arr2's order; values not in arr2 go at the end in ascending order.
c-relative-sort-array.hint: Count each value, emit arr2's values in order, then the rest ascending (counting sort works).

c-sort-by-frequency-asc.title: Sort Array by Increasing Frequency
description: Sort nums by how often each value occurs, least frequent first. Values with the same frequency go in decreasing order.
c-sort-by-frequency-asc.hint: Count, then sort with the comparator (count asc, value desc).

c-largest-number.title: Largest Number
description: Arrange the non-negative integers in nums to form the largest possible number and return it as a string (no leading zeros, so [0, 0] gives "0").
c-largest-number.hint: Compare two numbers as strings: put a before b if a + b > b + a.

c-h-index.title: H-Index
description: citations[i] is the citations of paper i. The h-index is the largest h such that at least h papers have at least h citations each. Return it.
c-h-index.hint: Sort descending; h is the last position i (1-based) with citations >= i.

c-meeting-rooms.title: Meeting Rooms
description: Given meeting time intervals [start, end), return true if one person can attend all of them (no two overlap; one ending at t and another starting at t is fine).
c-meeting-rooms.hint: Sort by start; any meeting starting before the previous one ends is a clash.

c-meeting-rooms-ii.title: Meeting Rooms II
description: Given meeting intervals [start, end), return the minimum number of rooms needed so no two meetings in a room overlap.
c-meeting-rooms-ii.hint: Sort starts and ends separately and sweep: a start before the earliest end needs a new room. Or a min-heap of end times.

c-non-overlapping-intervals.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap. Touching intervals like [1,2] and [2,3] don't overlap.
c-non-overlapping-intervals.hint: Sort by end and greedily keep each interval that starts after the last kept one ends.

c-insert-interval.title: Insert Interval
description: intervals is sorted and non-overlapping. Insert newInterval, merging where needed, and return the sorted non-overlapping result.
c-insert-interval.hint: Copy intervals ending before it, merge the overlapping ones into it, copy the rest.

c-sort-the-people.title: Sort the People
description: heights are distinct. Return the names sorted by height, tallest first.
c-sort-the-people.hint: Sort indices by height descending, then map to names.

c-maximum-gap.title: Maximum Gap
description: Return the largest difference between two successive elements of nums in sorted order, or 0 if nums has fewer than two elements. Try to do it in linear time.
c-maximum-gap.hint: Sorting works in O(n log n). Linear: bucket by (max - min) / (n - 1); the gap is between buckets.

c-array-partition.title: Array Partition
description: Group the 2n integers into n pairs to maximise the sum of min(a, b) over all pairs. Return that sum.
c-array-partition.hint: Sort and pair neighbours: take every other element.

c-minimum-absolute-difference.title: Minimum Absolute Difference
description: arr has distinct integers. Return all pairs [a, b] (a < b) with the minimum absolute difference, in ascending order.
c-minimum-absolute-difference.hint: Sort; only adjacent elements can be closest.

c-height-checker.title: Height Checker
description: Students should stand in non-decreasing order of height. Return how many indices hold the wrong height compared with the sorted order.
c-height-checker.hint: Compare with a sorted copy (counting sort since heights are small).

c-largest-perimeter-triangle.title: Largest Perimeter Triangle
description: Return the largest perimeter of a triangle with non-zero area formed from three of the lengths, or 0 if none can be formed.
c-largest-perimeter-triangle.hint: Sort descending; the first three consecutive values with a[i] < a[i+1] + a[i+2] win.

c-custom-sort-string.title: Custom Sort String
description: order has distinct letters. Permute s so its letters that appear in order follow that order; letters not in order go at the end, in their original relative order.
c-custom-sort-string.hint: Count letters of s, emit them in order's sequence, then the rest.

c-sort-by-parity-ii.title: Sort Array by Parity II
description: Half of nums is even and half odd. Put evens at even indices and odds at odd indices, keeping each group's original order.
c-sort-by-parity-ii.hint: Two write pointers: one for even slots, one for odd slots.

c-rank-transform.title: Rank Transform of an Array
description: Replace each element by its rank: the smallest value gets 1, equal values share a rank, and ranks are consecutive.
c-rank-transform.hint: Sort distinct values and map each to its position + 1.

c-smaller-than-current.title: How Many Numbers Are Smaller Than the Current Number
description: For each nums[i], count how many values in nums are strictly smaller.
c-smaller-than-current.hint: Sort a copy; the first index of each value is its answer (or counting sort since values are small).

c-reorder-log-files.title: Reorder Data in Log Files
description: Each log is an identifier followed by words. Letter-logs (words are letters) come first, sorted by content then identifier; digit-logs (words are digits) follow in their original order.
c-reorder-log-files.hint: Split off the identifier; sort letter-logs with the key (content, id) and append digit-logs as they were.

c-max-product-three.title: Maximum Product of Three Numbers
description: Return the maximum product of three numbers in nums.
c-max-product-three.hint: After sorting: max(three largest, two smallest x largest).

c-min-moves-equal-ii.title: Minimum Moves to Equal Array Elements II
description: A move increments or decrements one element by 1. Return the minimum moves to make all elements equal.
c-min-moves-equal-ii.hint: Everything should move to the median.

c-count-smaller-after-self.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description: Return counts where counts[i] is how many elements to the right of nums[i] are smaller than it.
c-count-smaller-after-self.hint: Merge sort with indices: while merging, count how many right-half elements jumped ahead of each left element.

c-car-fleet.title: Car Fleet
description: Cars drive toward target on a one-lane road; a car can't pass the one ahead but can catch up and then travel together as a fleet. Return how many fleets arrive at target.
c-car-fleet.hint: Sort by position descending and compare arrival times; a slower car ahead absorbs those behind it.

c-sort-matrix-diagonally.title: Sort the Matrix Diagonally
description: Sort every top-left to bottom-right diagonal of mat in ascending order and return the matrix.
c-sort-matrix-diagonally.hint: Cells on one diagonal share r - c. Collect, sort and write back per diagonal.

c-sort-by-bits.title: Sort Integers by the Number of 1 Bits
description: Sort arr by the number of 1 bits in each value, and by value when the counts are equal.

c-lower-bound.title: Lower Bound
description: nums is sorted. Return the first index i with nums[i] >= x, or nums.length if there is none.
c-lower-bound.hint: If nums[mid] >= x, mid could be the answer: record it and go left.

c-upper-bound.title: Upper Bound
description: nums is sorted. Return the first index i with nums[i] > x, or nums.length if there is none.
c-upper-bound.hint: Same as lower bound with > instead of >=.

c-floor-and-ceil.title: Floor and Ceil in a Sorted Array
description: nums is sorted. Return [floor, ceil]: the largest value <= x and the smallest value >= x. Use -1 for a missing one.
c-floor-and-ceil.hint: Two binary searches, or one that tracks both candidates.

c-count-occurrences.title: Count Occurrences in a Sorted Array
description: nums is sorted. Return how many times x appears, in O(log n).

c-search-rotated-ii.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
description: nums was sorted (with possible duplicates) then rotated. Return true if target is in nums.
c-search-rotated-ii.hint: Like the distinct version, but when nums[lo] == nums[mid] == nums[hi] you can only shrink both ends by one.

c-rotation-count.title: Find Out How Many Times an Array Has Been Rotated
description: A sorted array of distinct values was rotated right k times. Return k (the index of the minimum).
c-rotation-count.hint: Binary search for the minimum, as in Minimum in a Rotated Sorted Array.

c-single-element-sorted.title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
description: nums is sorted; every value appears exactly twice except one that appears once. Return it in O(log n).
