c-single-element-sorted.hint: Before the single element, pairs start at even indices; after it, at odd indices.

c-peak-in-mountain.title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
description: arr strictly increases then strictly decreases. Return the index of its peak in O(log n).
c-peak-in-mountain.hint: If arr[mid] < arr[mid + 1] the peak is to the right; otherwise it's at mid or to the left.

c-nth-root.title: Find the Nth Root of an Integer
description: Return the integer x with x^n == m, or -1 if no such integer exists.
c-nth-root.hint: Binary search x in [1, m]; compute x^n with early exit to avoid overflow.

c-min-days-bouquets.title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
description: Flower i blooms on day bloomDay[i]. A bouquet needs k adjacent bloomed flowers. Return the minimum day to make m bouquets, or -1 if impossible.
c-min-days-bouquets.hint: Binary search the day; for a day d, count bouquets by scanning runs of bloomed flowers.

c-smallest-divisor.title: Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
description: Choose a positive integer divisor, divide every element by it rounding up, and sum the results. Return the smallest divisor whose sum is at most threshold.
c-smallest-divisor.hint: The sum shrinks as the divisor grows: binary search it.

c-ship-within-days.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
description: Packages must ship in the given order; each day the ship carries packages up to its capacity. Return the least capacity that ships everything within days.
c-ship-within-days.hint: Search capacity in [max(weights), sum(weights)]; count days greedily.

c-kth-missing-positive.title: Kth Missing Positive Number
description: arr is strictly increasing positive integers. Return the k-th positive integer missing from arr.
c-kth-missing-positive.hint: Missing count before index i is arr[i] - (i + 1); binary search where it reaches k.

c-aggressive-cows.title: Aggressive Cows
description: Place k cows in the stalls (positions given) so the minimum distance between any two cows is as large as possible. Return that distance.
c-aggressive-cows.hint: Binary search the distance; greedily place cows left to right.

c-book-allocation.title: Allocate Minimum Number of Pages
description: Give each student a contiguous block of books (at least one each, every book assigned). Minimise the maximum pages any student reads. Return it, or -1 if there are more students than books.
c-book-allocation.hint: Binary search the maximum pages; count students greedily.

c-split-array-largest-sum.title: Split Array Largest Sum
description: Split nums into k non-empty contiguous subarrays so that the largest subarray sum is as small as possible. Return that sum.
c-split-array-largest-sum.hint: Same pattern as book allocation (and the painter's partition).

c-kth-element-two-sorted.title: K-th Element of Two Sorted Arrays
description: Return the k-th smallest element (1-based) of the union of two sorted arrays. Aim for O(log(min(n, m))).
c-kth-element-two-sorted.hint: Binary search how many elements to take from the smaller array, like median of two sorted arrays.

c-row-with-max-ones.title: Row with Maximum Ones
description: Each row of the binary matrix is sorted (0s then 1s). Return the index of the row with the most 1s (the first such row), or -1 if there are no 1s.
c-row-with-max-ones.hint: Count 1s per row with lower bound of 1, or walk a staircase from the top-right.

c-search-2d-matrix.title: Search a 2D Matrix
description: Rows are sorted, and each row's first value is greater than the previous row's last. Return true if target is in the matrix, in O(log(m * n)).
c-search-2d-matrix.hint: Treat it as one sorted array of m * n: index i is matrix[i / n][i % n].

c-search-2d-matrix-ii.title: Search a 2D Matrix II
description: Each row is sorted left to right and each column top to bottom. Return true if target is in the matrix.
c-search-2d-matrix-ii.hint: Start at the top-right corner: go left if it's too big, down if too small.

c-median-row-sorted-matrix.title: Median in a Row-wise Sorted Matrix
description: Each row of the matrix is sorted and the total number of elements is odd. Return the median, without flattening and sorting everything.
c-median-row-sorted-matrix.hint: Binary search the value: count elements <= mid with upper bound in each row.

c-next-greatest-letter.title: Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target
description: letters is a sorted string of lowercase letters; target is one letter. Return the smallest letter in letters that is strictly greater than target, wrapping around to the first letter if there is none.
c-next-greatest-letter.hint: Upper bound on the target; wrap to index 0 at the end.

c-print-1-to-n.title: Numbers 1 to N with Recursion
description: Return [1, 2, ..., n] built with recursion (no loops).
c-print-1-to-n.hint: Solve n - 1 first, then append n.

c-print-n-to-1.title: Numbers N to 1 with Recursion
description: Return [n, n - 1, ..., 1] built with recursion (no loops).
c-print-n-to-1.hint: Put n first, then recurse on n - 1.

c-reverse-array-recursive.title: Reverse an Array with Recursion
description: Reverse nums using recursion: swap the ends, then recurse on the inside.
c-reverse-array-recursive.hint: reverse(l, r): swap nums[l], nums[r], then reverse(l + 1, r - 1); stop when l >= r.

c-palindrome-recursive.title: Check Palindrome with Recursion
description: Return true if s reads the same forwards and backwards (exact characters), using recursion.
c-palindrome-recursive.hint: Compare s[i] with s[n - 1 - i] and recurse on i + 1 until the middle.

c-count-good-numbers.title: Count Good Numbers
description: A digit string is good if digits at even indices are even (0,2,4,6,8) and digits at odd indices are prime (2,3,5,7). Return how many good digit strings of length n exist, modulo 1,000,000,007.
c-count-good-numbers.hint: Answer = 5^ceil(n/2) * 4^floor(n/2). Write fast power recursively: x^n = (x^(n/2))^2 (times x if n is odd). Use long.

c-sort-stack-recursive.title: Sort a Stack with Recursion
description: stack is given bottom to top. Sort it so the smallest value is at the bottom, using only recursion and push/pop (no loops, no extra data structure). Return it bottom to top.
c-sort-stack-recursive.hint: Pop the top, sort the rest recursively, then insert the popped value into its place recursively.

c-reverse-stack-recursive.title: Reverse a Stack with Recursion
description: stack is given bottom to top. Reverse it using only recursion and push/pop. Return it bottom to top.
c-reverse-stack-recursive.hint: Pop the top, reverse the rest, then insert the popped value at the bottom (another recursion).

c-tower-of-hanoi.title: Tower of Hanoi
description: Move n disks from rod 1 to rod 3 using rod 2, one disk at a time, never placing a larger disk on a smaller one. Return the moves as [from, to] pairs in order (the standard minimal sequence).
c-tower-of-hanoi.hint: Move n - 1 disks to the helper rod, move the largest, then move n - 1 disks on top of it.

c-pascal-row.title: Pascal's Triangle Row
description: Return row rowIndex (0-based) of Pascal's triangle.
c-pascal-row.hint: Build each row from the previous one, or use C(r, k) = C(r, k - 1) * (r - k + 1) / k.

c-kth-symbol-grammar.title: K-th Symbol in Grammar
description: Row 1 is "0". Each next row replaces 0 with 01 and 1 with 10. Return the k-th (1-based) symbol of row n.
c-kth-symbol-grammar.hint: Symbol k of row n comes from symbol ceil(k/2) of row n - 1, flipped if k is even.

c-find-the-winner.title: Find the Winner of the Circular Game
description: n friends sit in a circle numbered 1..n. Counting k clockwise (including the current friend) removes that friend; counting continues from the next one. Return the winner.

c-decode-string.title: Decode String
description: Decode s where k[encoded] means encoded repeated k times. Brackets may nest.
c-decode-string.hint: Recursively decode the inside of each bracket, or use a stack of (count, built-so-far).

c-binary-strings-no-consecutive-ones.title: Binary Strings Without Consecutive 1s
description: Return every binary string of length n with no two adjacent 1s, in lexicographic order.
c-binary-strings-no-consecutive-ones.hint: Recurse adding '0' always and '1' only if the last character isn't '1'. Adding '0' first keeps the order.

c-steps-to-zero.title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
description: If num is even, divide it by 2; otherwise subtract 1. Return how many steps until it reaches 0.
c-steps-to-zero.hint: steps(n) = 0 if n == 0, else 1 + steps(n / 2 or n - 1).

c-gray-code.title: Gray Code
description: Return the standard n-bit reflected Gray code sequence starting at 0 (2^n values, consecutive values differ in one bit).
c-gray-code.hint: gray(n) = gray(n - 1) followed by gray(n - 1) reversed with the top bit set.

c-different-ways-parentheses.title: Different Ways to Add Parentheses
description: expression has numbers and the operators +, - and *. Return every result you can get by adding parentheses in all possible ways, sorted ascending (duplicates kept).
c-different-ways-parentheses.hint: Split at each operator, recurse on both sides, combine every pair of results.

c-elimination-game.title: Elimination Game
description: Start with 1..n. Remove every other number from left to right starting with the first, then every other from right to left, alternating until one number is left. Return it.
c-elimination-game.hint: Track the head, the step and the count; the head moves when going left-to-right or when the count is odd.

c-count-and-say.title: Count and Say
description: countAndSay(1) = "1"; countAndSay(n) reads countAndSay(n - 1) aloud as runs: "21" is one 2 then one 1, so the next term is "1211". Return the n-th term.
c-count-and-say.hint: Recursively build term n - 1, then encode its runs.

c-subset-xor-sum.title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
description: Return the sum of the XOR of every subset of nums (the empty subset's XOR is 0).
c-subset-xor-sum.hint: Recurse with (index, xorSoFar): include or skip nums[index].

c-predict-the-winner.title: Predict the Winner
description: Two players alternately take a number from either end of nums, player 1 first, both playing optimally. Return true if player 1's total is at least player 2's.
c-predict-the-winner.hint: best(l, r) = max(nums[l] - best(l + 1, r), nums[r] - best(l, r - 1)): your lead over the opponent.

c-integer-replacement.title: Integer Replacement
description: If n is even, replace it with n / 2; if odd, with n + 1 or n - 1. Return the fewest replacements to reach 1.
c-integer-replacement.hint: Recurse on both choices for odd n with memoisation (use long for n + 1).

c-remove-all-occurrences.title: Remove All Occurrences of a Substring
description: Repeatedly remove the leftmost occurrence of part from s until none remains. Return the result.
c-remove-all-occurrences.hint: Remove the first match and recurse, or build with a stack and check its end.

c-strobogrammatic-ii.title: Strobogrammatic Number II
description: A strobogrammatic number looks the same rotated 180 degrees (0, 1, 8 map to themselves; 6 and 9 swap). Return all of length n without leading zeros (except "0" itself), sorted.
c-strobogrammatic-ii.hint: Build from the middle out: wrap each length n - 2 answer with the pairs 00, 11, 69, 88, 96 (no 00 on the outermost layer).

c-recursive-digit-sum.title: Super Digit
description: Concatenate the digit string n k times to get p. The super digit of a number is itself if it has one digit, otherwise the super digit of the sum of its digits. Return the super digit of p.
c-recursive-digit-sum.hint: Sum n's digits once and multiply by k, then recurse on the digit sum of that number.

c-unique-digit-numbers.title: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
description: Return how many integers x with 0 <= x < 10^n have no repeated digit.
c-unique-digit-numbers.hint: count(k digits) = 9 * 9 * 8 * ... (k factors); add them up for k = 1..n plus 1 for zero.

c-next-greater-element-i.title: Next Greater Element I
description: nums1 is a subset of nums2 (distinct values). For each x in nums1, find the first value greater than x to its right in nums2, or -1.
c-next-greater-element-i.hint: Monotonic stack over nums2 fills a map value -> next greater.

c-next-greater-element-ii.title: Next Greater Element II
description: nums is circular. For each element, return the first greater value found by moving forward (wrapping around), or -1.
c-next-greater-element-ii.hint: Loop twice over the indices (i % n) with a stack of unresolved indices.

c-previous-smaller-element.title: Previous Smaller Element
description: For each element, return the nearest value to its left that is strictly smaller, or -1.
c-previous-smaller-element.hint: Keep an increasing stack; pop values >= the current one.

c-stock-span.title: Online Stock Span
description: The span of today's price is how many consecutive days, ending today, the price was <= today's price. Return the span for every day.
c-stock-span.hint: Stack of (price, span) pairs; merge spans of smaller prices.

c-largest-rectangle-histogram.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description: heights are bars of width 1. Return the area of the largest rectangle inside the histogram.
c-largest-rectangle-histogram.hint: For each bar, the widest rectangle of its height spans to the previous and next smaller bars.

c-maximal-rectangle.title: Maximal Rectangle
description: matrix holds 0s and 1s. Return the area of the largest rectangle containing only 1s.
c-maximal-rectangle.hint: Row by row, build histogram heights and reuse Largest Rectangle in Histogram.

c-asteroid-collision.title: Asteroid Collision
description: Positive asteroids move right, negative move left, all at the same speed. When two meet, the smaller one explodes (both if equal). Return the asteroids left after all collisions.
c-asteroid-collision.hint: Stack: a left-moving asteroid fights right-moving ones on top of the stack.

c-remove-k-digits.title: Remove K Digits
description: Remove k digits from the number string num to make the smallest possible number. Return it without leading zeros ("0" if empty).
c-remove-k-digits.hint: Greedy with an increasing stack: pop a larger previous digit while you still have removals.

c-sum-subarray-minimums.title: Sum of Subarray Minimums
description: Return the sum of min(b) over every contiguous subarray b of arr, modulo 1,000,000,007.
c-sum-subarray-minimums.hint: Each a[i] is the minimum of (i - prevLess) * (nextLessOrEqual - i) subarrays.

c-sum-subarray-ranges.title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
description: The range of a subarray is its max minus its min. Return the sum of ranges of all subarrays.
c-sum-subarray-ranges.hint: (sum of subarray maximums) - (sum of subarray minimums), each with monotonic stacks.

c-simplify-path.title: Simplify Path
description: Convert an absolute Unix path to its canonical form: single slashes, no trailing slash, '.' removed and '..' going up one directory (never above root).
c-simplify-path.hint: Split on '/', push names, pop on '..', ignore '' and '.'.

c-basic-calculator-ii.title: Basic Calculator II
description: Evaluate s containing non-negative integers, +, -, *, / and spaces. Division truncates toward zero. No parentheses.
c-basic-calculator-ii.hint: Push numbers on a stack; apply * and / immediately to the top, push negatives for -. Sum the stack.

c-min-add-valid-parentheses.title: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
description: Return the minimum number of '(' or ')' insertions needed to make s a valid parentheses string.
c-min-add-valid-parentheses.hint: Track open count; an unmatched ')' needs an insertion. Add the leftover opens.

c-score-of-parentheses.title: Score of Parentheses
description: s is balanced. "()" scores 1, AB scores A + B, and (A) scores 2 * A. Return the score of s.

c-longest-valid-parentheses.title: Longest Valid Parentheses
description: Return the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring of s.
c-longest-valid-parentheses.hint: Stack of indices with a base marker; the length is i - stack top after a match.

c-make-string-great.title: Make The String Great
description: Repeatedly remove two adjacent characters that are the same letter in different cases (like 'a' and 'A'). Return the final string.
c-make-string-great.hint: Stack: pop when the top is the same letter with the opposite case.

c-remove-duplicate-letters.title: Remove Duplicate Letters
description: Remove duplicate letters so every letter appears once, and the result is the smallest in lexicographic order among all such results.
c-remove-duplicate-letters.hint: Greedy stack: pop a larger letter if it appears again later; skip letters already in the stack.

c-validate-stack-sequences.title: Validate Stack Sequences
description: pushed and popped are permutations of distinct values. Return true if they could be the result of push and pop operations on an initially empty stack.
c-validate-stack-sequences.hint: Simulate: push each value, then pop while the top matches the next value to pop.

c-time-to-buy-tickets.title: Time Needed to Buy Tickets
description: People queue to buy tickets; tickets[i] is how many person i wants. Each second the front person buys one ticket and, if they need more, goes to the back. Return the seconds until person k finishes.
c-time-to-buy-tickets.hint: Simulate with a queue, or note person i before k buys min(t[i], t[k]) and after k buys min(t[i], t[k] - 1).

c-dota2-senate.title: Dota2 Senate
description: Senators from Radiant ('R') and Dire ('D') vote in order; each can ban one opposing senator. Banned senators lose all rights. Rounds repeat until one party remains. Return "Radiant" or "Dire".
c-dota2-senate.hint: Two queues of indices; the smaller index bans the other and re-enters with index + n.

c-reveal-cards-increasing.title: Reveal Cards in Increasing Order
description: Cards (distinct values) are revealed by: take the top card, then move the next top card to the bottom, repeating. Return an ordering of deck so the cards are revealed in increasing order.
c-reveal-cards-increasing.hint: Simulate the reveal on a queue of positions 0..n-1 and drop sorted cards into them.

c-students-unable-to-eat.title: Number of Students Unable to Eat Lunch
description: Students (0 or 1, their preferred sandwich) queue; sandwiches form a stack (index 0 on top). The front student takes the top sandwich if it matches, otherwise goes to the back. Return how many students can't eat.
c-students-unable-to-eat.hint: Order doesn't matter for students: count preferences, and stop at the first sandwich nobody left wants.

c-132-pattern.title: 132 Pattern
description: Return true if there are i < j < k with nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j].
c-132-pattern.hint: Scan from the right with a decreasing stack; track the best "2" popped so far.

c-crawler-log-folder.title: Crawler Log Folder
description: A file system starts at the main folder. "../" moves to the parent (stays at main if already there), "./" stays, "x/" moves into child x. Return how many steps it takes to get back to main afterwards.
c-crawler-log-folder.hint: Only the depth matters: it's a stack's size.

c-remove-list-elements.title: Remove Linked List Elements
description: Remove every node whose value equals val and return the new head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-remove-list-elements.hint: A dummy node before head makes removing the head the same as any other node.

c-list-length.title: Length of a Linked List
description: Return the number of nodes in the list.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-list-length.hint: Walk the list with a pointer, counting nodes until null.

c-search-in-list.title: Search in a Linked List
description: Return true if some node holds key.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-search-in-list.hint: Traverse until you find key or reach null.

c-insert-at-position.title: Insert into a Linked List
description: Insert a new node with value val so it ends up at index pos (0 = new head; pos equal to the length appends). Return the head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-insert-at-position.hint: Walk to the node before position pos and splice the new node in; pos 0 replaces the head.

c-delete-at-position.title: Delete a Node at a Position
description: Delete the node at index pos (0-based, always valid) and return the head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-delete-at-position.hint: Stop at the node before pos and set its next to next.next.

c-rotate-list.title: Rotate List
description: Rotate the list to the right by k places and return the new head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-rotate-list.hint: Find the length and tail, join tail to head, then cut at length - k % length.

c-reverse-list-ii.title: Reverse Linked List II
description: Reverse the nodes from position left to position right (1-based, inclusive) and return the head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-reverse-list-ii.hint: Walk to the node before left, then repeatedly move the next node to the front of the reversed part.

c-swap-nodes-in-pairs.title: Swap Nodes in Pairs
description: Swap every two adjacent nodes (swap the nodes, not just the values) and return the head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-swap-nodes-in-pairs.hint: With a dummy: point prev at second, first at the rest, second at first; move prev two nodes on.

c-reverse-k-group.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
description: Reverse the nodes of the list k at a time. A final group with fewer than k nodes stays as it is.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-reverse-k-group.hint: Check that k nodes remain, reverse them, connect to the previous group's tail, repeat.

c-sort-list.title: Sort List
description: Sort the list in ascending order. Aim for O(n log n) time (merge sort on the list).
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-sort-list.hint: Split at the middle with slow/fast pointers, sort both halves, merge.

c-partition-list.title: Partition List
description: Rearrange the list so all nodes with value less than x come before nodes with value >= x, keeping the original order within each part.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-partition-list.hint: Build two lists (less, rest) with dummy heads and join them.

c-remove-duplicates-ii-list.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
description: The list is sorted. Delete every node whose value is duplicated, keeping only values that appear once.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-remove-duplicates-ii-list.hint: With a dummy: when a run of equal values starts, skip the whole run.

c-add-two-numbers-ii.title: Add Two Numbers II
description: Each list stores a non-negative number with its most significant digit first. Return their sum as a list in the same order.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-add-two-numbers-ii.hint: Push digits on two stacks (or reverse both lists), add from the back with a carry.

c-sort-012-list.title: Sort a Linked List of 0s, 1s and 2s
description: The list holds only 0, 1 and 2. Sort it by relinking nodes (not by counting and overwriting).
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-sort-012-list.hint: Three dummy lists for 0s, 1s and 2s; join them at the end.

c-reorder-list.title: Reorder List
description: Reorder L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln into L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> ... and return the head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-reorder-list.hint: Find the middle, reverse the second half, then weave the two halves together.

c-delete-middle-node.title: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
description: Delete the middle node (index floor(n / 2), 0-based) and return the head. A single-node list becomes empty.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-delete-middle-node.hint: Slow/fast pointers, with slow stopping one node before the middle.

c-double-a-number.title: Double a Number Represented as a Linked List
description: The list holds a non-negative number's digits, most significant first (no leading zeros except 0 itself). Return the list for twice that number.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-double-a-number.hint: A digit's carry depends only on whether the next digit is >= 5, so one forward pass works.

c-merge-nodes-between-zeros.title: Merge Nodes in Between Zeros
description: The list starts and ends with 0 and has no two consecutive 0s. Replace each group of nodes between two 0s by one node holding their sum, and remove the 0s.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-merge-nodes-between-zeros.hint: Walk the list summing values; at each 0, emit the sum.

c-binary-list-to-integer.title: Convert Binary Number in a Linked List to Integer
description: Each node holds a bit, most significant first. Return the number's decimal value.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-binary-list-to-integer.hint: value = value * 2 + node.val for each node.

c-remove-nodes-greater-right.title: Remove Nodes From Linked List
description: Remove every node that has a node with a strictly greater value anywhere to its right.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-remove-nodes-greater-right.hint: Reverse, keep a running maximum dropping smaller nodes, reverse back. Or a monotonic stack.

c-swap-kth-nodes.title: Swapping Nodes in a Linked List
description: Swap the values of the k-th node from the start and the k-th node from the end (1-based) and return the head.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-swap-kth-nodes.hint: A pointer k - 1 steps ahead, then move both until the lead reaches the end.

c-maximum-twin-sum.title: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List
description: The list has even length n. Node i and node n - 1 - i are twins. Return the maximum twin sum.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-maximum-twin-sum.hint: Reverse the second half, then walk both halves together.

c-insert-gcd-nodes.title: Insert Greatest Common Divisors in Linked List
description: Between every pair of adjacent nodes, insert a node holding their greatest common divisor.
The list is given as values in order; your function receives its head ListNode (fields val and next).
c-insert-gcd-nodes.hint: For each node with a next, splice in new ListNode(gcd(a, b)) and skip over it.

c-transpose-matrix.title: Transpose Matrix
description: Return the transpose of matrix: rows become columns.
c-transpose-matrix.hint: result[c][r] = matrix[r][c]; the result is cols x rows.

c-flip-invert-image.title: Flipping an Image
description: image is binary. Flip each row horizontally, then invert it (0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0). Return the result.
c-flip-invert-image.hint: Two pointers per row: swap and invert in one pass.

c-reshape-matrix.title: Reshape the Matrix
description: Reshape mat into r rows and c columns, filling row by row in the original row-major order. If that's impossible, return mat unchanged.
c-reshape-matrix.hint: Element number k goes to row k / c, column k % c.

c-toeplitz-matrix.title: Toeplitz Matrix
description: Return true if every top-left to bottom-right diagonal has a single repeated value.
c-toeplitz-matrix.hint: Each cell must equal its upper-left neighbour.

c-lucky-numbers-matrix.title: Lucky Numbers in a Matrix
description: Values are distinct. A lucky number is the minimum of its row and the maximum of its column. Return all lucky numbers in increasing order.
c-lucky-numbers-matrix.hint: Intersect the set of row minimums with the set of column maximums.

c-richest-customer-wealth.title: Richest Customer Wealth
description: accounts[i][j] is the money customer i has in bank j. Return the wealth of the richest customer.
c-richest-customer-wealth.hint: Sum each row; take the maximum.

c-count-negatives.title: Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix
description: Rows and columns of grid are sorted in non-increasing order. Return how many values are negative, ideally in O(m + n).
c-count-negatives.hint: Staircase from the bottom-left: move right past non-negatives, count the rest of the row, move up.

c-cells-with-odd-values.title: Cells with Odd Values in a Matrix
description: Start with an m x n matrix of zeros. Each [r, c] in indices adds 1 to every cell in row r and every cell in column c. Return how many cells end up odd.
c-cells-with-odd-values.hint: Only the parity of each row and column count matters.

c-spiral-matrix-ii.title: Spiral Matrix II
description: Return an n x n matrix filled with 1 to n^2 in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left.
c-spiral-matrix-ii.hint: Walk the four boundaries as in Spiral Order, writing an increasing counter.

c-island-perimeter.title: Island Perimeter
description: grid has exactly one island of 1s (connected up, down, left, right) and no lakes. Return the island's perimeter.
c-island-perimeter.hint: Each land cell adds 4, minus 1 for every land neighbour.

c-image-smoother.title: Image Smoother
description: Replace each cell by the floor of the average of itself and its up-to-8 neighbours that exist. Return the new image.
c-image-smoother.hint: For each cell, loop over the 3 x 3 block clipped to the grid.

c-matrix-block-sum.title: Matrix Block Sum
description: answer[i][j] is the sum of mat[r][c] for every cell with |r - i| <= k and |c - j| <= k (inside the grid). Return answer.
c-matrix-block-sum.hint: 2D prefix sums turn each block into four lookups.

c-max-hourglass-sum.title: Maximum Sum of an Hourglass
description: An hourglass is a 3 x 3 block without its middle-left and middle-right cells. Return the maximum hourglass sum in the grid (at least 3 x 3).
c-max-hourglass-sum.hint: Try every top-left corner; seven cells per hourglass.

c-diagonal-traverse.title: Diagonal Traverse
description: Return all elements in zigzag diagonal order: up-right along the first diagonal, then down-left along the next, alternating.
c-diagonal-traverse.hint: Cells on diagonal d have r + c = d; reverse every even diagonal.

c-rotation-equal.title: Determine Whether Matrix Can Be Obtained By Rotation
description: Return true if rotating the square matrix mat by some multiple of 90 degrees gives target.
c-rotation-equal.hint: Rotate up to three times and compare after each.

c-count-square-submatrices.title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
description: matrix is binary. Return how many square submatrices consist entirely of 1s.
c-count-square-submatrices.hint: dp[r][c] = 1 + min(up, left, up-left) for a 1: it's both the largest square there and how many end there.

c-maximal-square.title: Maximal Square
description: matrix is binary. Return the area of the largest square containing only 1s.
c-maximal-square.hint: Same dp as counting squares; answer is (max dp)^2.

c-shift-2d-grid.title: Shift 2D Grid
description: Shift every element one step to the right k times; the last element of a row moves to the next row's start, and the bottom-right moves to the top-left. Return the grid.
c-shift-2d-grid.hint: Flatten conceptually: the element at index i moves to (i + k) % (m * n).

c-largest-local-values.title: Largest Local Values in a Matrix
description: For an n x n grid, return an (n - 2) x (n - 2) matrix whose [i][j] is the largest value in the 3 x 3 block starting at grid[i][j].
c-largest-local-values.hint: Brute force over each 3 x 3 block is fine at this size.

c-ones-minus-zeros.title: Difference Between Ones and Zeros in Row and Column
description: grid is binary. diff[i][j] = onesRow_i + onesCol_j - zerosRow_i - zerosCol_j. Return diff.
c-ones-minus-zeros.hint: Precompute ones per row and per column; zeros are length minus ones.

c-projection-area.title: Projection Area of 3D Shapes
description: grid[i][j] is a tower of cubes. Return the total area of the shadows seen from the top, the front and the side.
c-projection-area.hint: Top: non-zero cells. Front: column maxima. Side: row maxima.

c-score-after-flipping.title: Score After Flipping Matrix
description: grid is binary. A move flips an entire row or column. Each row is read as a binary number. Return the highest possible sum of these numbers.
c-score-after-flipping.hint: Make every row start with 1, then flip any column where 1s are the minority.

c-spiral-matrix-iii.title: Spiral Matrix III
description: Starting at (rStart, cStart) facing east, walk a clockwise spiral that grows outward (it may leave the grid and come back). Return the coordinates of every grid cell in the order you visit them.
c-spiral-matrix-iii.hint: Step lengths go 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, ... turning right after each run; record cells inside the grid.

c-check-row-col-all-numbers.title: Check if Every Row and Column Contains All Numbers
description: An n x n matrix is valid if every row and every column contains all integers 1..n. Return whether it is valid.
c-check-row-col-all-numbers.hint: A set (or boolean array) per row and per column.

c-check-kth-bit.title: Check if the K-th Bit Is Set
description: Return true if bit k (0 = least significant) of the non-negative integer n is 1.

c-set-kth-bit.title: Set the K-th Bit
description: Return n with bit k (0 = least significant) set to 1.

c-toggle-kth-bit.title: Toggle the K-th Bit
description: Return n with bit k (0 = least significant) flipped.

c-swap-without-temp.title: Swap Two Numbers Without a Temporary Variable
description: Return [b, a], swapping the values with XOR (no third variable).
c-swap-without-temp.hint: a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b.

c-single-number-ii.title: Single Number II
description: Every value in nums appears three times except one, which appears once. Return it in O(n) time and O(1) space.
c-single-number-ii.hint: Count each bit position modulo 3; the leftover bits form the answer.

c-single-number-iii.title: Single Number III
description: Exactly two values in nums appear once; all others appear twice. Return the two values in increasing order.
c-single-number-iii.hint: XOR everything to get a ^ b; split the numbers by any set bit of it and XOR each group.

c-reverse-bits.title: Reverse Bits
description: Reverse the 32 bits of n and return the result. (Inputs are even, so the answer fits in a signed 32-bit int.)

c-hamming-distance.title: Hamming Distance
description: Return the number of bit positions where x and y differ.
c-hamming-distance.hint: Count the set bits of x ^ y.

c-xor-1-to-n.title: XOR of Numbers from 1 to N
description: Return 1 ^ 2 ^ ... ^ n in O(1).
c-xor-1-to-n.hint: The XOR prefix repeats every 4: n, 1, n + 1, 0 for n % 4 = 0, 1, 2, 3.

c-xor-l-to-r.title: XOR of Numbers in a Range
description: Return l ^ (l + 1) ^ ... ^ r.

c-divide-two-integers.title: Divide Two Integers
description: Divide without using *, / or %. Truncate toward zero. If the result overflows the 32-bit signed range, return 2^31 - 1.
c-divide-two-integers.hint: Work with longs (or negatives) and subtract the largest shifted divisor (divisor << k) that fits, adding 1 << k.

c-min-bit-flips.title: Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
description: Return the minimum number of single-bit flips to turn start into goal.

c-number-complement.title: Number Complement
description: Flip every bit of num's binary representation (no leading zeros) and return the result.
c-number-complement.hint: XOR with a mask of all 1s as long as num's bit length.

c-binary-gap.title: Binary Gap
description: Return the longest distance between two adjacent 1 bits of n (positions differ by the gap), or 0 if there are fewer than two 1s.
c-binary-gap.hint: Track the index of the last 1 seen while scanning bits.

c-range-bitwise-and.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
description: Return the bitwise AND of every number from left to right inclusive.
c-range-bitwise-and.hint: The answer is the common binary prefix of left and right.

c-total-hamming-distance.title: Total Hamming Distance
description: Return the sum of Hamming distances over every pair of values in nums.
c-total-hamming-distance.hint: For each bit, ones * zeros pairs differ there.

c-maximum-xor-pair.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
description: Return the maximum of nums[i] ^ nums[j] over all pairs (i may equal j).
c-maximum-xor-pair.hint: Build the answer bit by bit from the top with a prefix set, or use a binary trie.

c-sum-without-plus.title: Sum of Two Integers
description: Return a + b without using + or -.
c-sum-without-plus.hint: a ^ b adds without carry; (a & b) << 1 is the carry. Repeat until the carry is 0.

c-decode-xored-array.title: Decode XORed Array
description: encoded[i] = arr[i] ^ arr[i + 1]. Given encoded and arr[0] = first, return arr.

c-min-flips-or.title: Minimum Flips to Make a OR b Equal to c
description: Return the fewest single-bit flips in a and b so that a | b == c.
c-min-flips-or.hint: Bit by bit: if c's bit is 0, flip every 1 in a and b; if it's 1 and both are 0, flip one.

c-alternating-bits.title: Binary Number with Alternating Bits
description: Return true if adjacent bits of n always differ.
c-alternating-bits.hint: x = n ^ (n >> 1) must be all 1s: check x & (x + 1) == 0.

c-xor-operation-array.title: XOR Operation in an Array
description: nums[i] = start + 2 * i for i in 0..n-1. Return the XOR of all elements of nums.
c-xor-operation-array.hint: A direct loop is fine; there is also an O(1) formula.

c-prime-set-bits.title: Prime Number of Set Bits in Binary Representation
description: Count numbers in [left, right] whose number of set bits is a prime number.
c-prime-set-bits.hint: Bit counts are at most 20, so check against a small set of primes.

c-concatenated-binary.title: Concatenation of Consecutive Binary Numbers
description: Concatenate the binary representations of 1 to n in order and return that number modulo 1,000,000,007.
c-concatenated-binary.hint: Shift the running value left by the bit length of i, add i, take the modulo.

c-prefix-xor-original.title: Find the Original Array of Prefix Xor
description: pref[i] = arr[0] ^ arr[1] ^ ... ^ arr[i]. Return arr.

c-neighboring-xor.title: Neighboring Bitwise XOR
description: derived[i] = original[i] ^ original[(i + 1) % n] for some binary array original. Return true if such an original exists.
c-neighboring-xor.hint: XOR of all derived values equals original[0] ^ original[0] = 0.

c-lemonade-change.title: Lemonade Change
description: Each lemonade costs $5. Customers pay with $5, $10 or $20 bills in order, and you start with no change. Return true if you can give everyone correct change.
c-lemonade-change.hint: Track $5 and $10 counts; for $20 prefer giving one $10 + one $5.

c-jump-game-ii.title: Jump Game II
description: nums[i] is the maximum jump from index i. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index (it's always reachable).
c-jump-game-ii.hint: BFS by levels: track the end of the current jump's reach and the farthest next reach.

c-gas-station.title: Gas Station
description: Station i has gas[i]; driving to the next station costs cost[i]. Return the starting index to travel the circle once, or -1. The answer is unique if it exists.
c-gas-station.hint: If total gas >= total cost an answer exists; restart the candidate after any point where the tank goes negative.

c-candy.title: Candy
description: Each child gets at least one candy, and a child with a higher rating than a neighbour gets more candy than that neighbour. Return the minimum total.
c-candy.hint: Left-to-right pass for left neighbours, right-to-left pass for right neighbours, take the max per child.

c-partition-labels.title: Partition Labels
description: Split s into as many parts as possible so each letter appears in at most one part. Return the sizes of the parts in order.
c-partition-labels.hint: Record each letter's last index; cut when the current index equals the furthest last index seen.

c-min-arrows-balloons.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
description: Balloons span [xstart, xend] horizontally. An arrow shot at x bursts every balloon with xstart <= x <= xend. Return the minimum arrows to burst all.
c-min-arrows-balloons.hint: Sort by end; shoot at the first end and skip every balloon that starts by then.

c-valid-parenthesis-string.title: Valid Parenthesis String
description: s has '(', ')' and '*'. A '*' can be '(', ')' or empty. Return true if s can be valid.
c-valid-parenthesis-string.hint: Track the range [low, high] of possible open counts; fail if high < 0, clamp low at 0, valid if low == 0 at the end.

c-task-scheduler.title: Task Scheduler
description: tasks is a string of uppercase letters (one per task). Equal tasks must be at least n intervals apart; idle intervals are allowed. Return the fewest intervals to finish all tasks.
c-task-scheduler.hint: Frame around the most frequent task: (maxCount - 1) * (n + 1) + number of tasks with maxCount, at least len(tasks).

c-maximum-units-truck.title: Maximum Units on a Truck
description: boxTypes[i] = [numberOfBoxes, unitsPerBox]. The truck carries at most truckSize boxes. Return the maximum total units.
c-maximum-units-truck.hint: Take boxes with the most units first.

c-maximum-69-number.title: Maximum 69 Number
description: num has only digits 6 and 9. Change at most one digit (6 to 9 or 9 to 6) to get the largest number.

c-min-platforms.title: Minimum Number of Platforms
description: Train i arrives at arr[i] and departs at dep[i] (HHMM times). A platform can't hold two trains at once; a train arriving at the same minute another departs needs another platform. Return the minimum number of platforms.
c-min-platforms.hint: Sort arrivals and departures; sweep counting trains present.

c-job-sequencing.title: Job Sequencing Problem
description: Each job takes one unit of time and must finish by its deadline to earn its profit; one job at a time. Return [number of jobs done, maximum profit].
c-job-sequencing.hint: Sort by profit descending; put each job in the latest free slot at or before its deadline.

c-fractional-knapsack.title: Fractional Knapsack
description: Items have values and weights; you may take fractions of an item. Return the maximum total value that fits in capacity.
c-fractional-knapsack.hint: Take items by value/weight ratio, the last one possibly partly.

c-min-coins-greedy.title: Minimum Coins (Indian Currency)
description: Using denominations 2000, 500, 200, 100, 50, 20, 10, 5, 2 and 1, return the coins/notes that make amount with the fewest pieces, largest first.
c-min-coins-greedy.hint: Greedy works because these denominations are canonical: always take the largest that fits.

c-shortest-job-first.title: Shortest Job First (Average Waiting Time)
description: All processes arrive at time 0 with burst times bt. Run them shortest first and return the average waiting time, rounded down.
c-shortest-job-first.hint: Sort; each job waits for the sum of all shorter jobs before it.

c-two-city-scheduling.title: Two City Scheduling
description: 2n people; costs[i] = [costA, costB] to fly person i to city A or B. Exactly n go to each city. Return the minimum total cost.
c-two-city-scheduling.hint: Sort by costA - costB; send the first half to A.

c-hand-of-straights.title: Hand of Straights
description: Return true if the cards can be split into groups of groupSize consecutive values.
c-hand-of-straights.hint: Take the smallest remaining card and try to build its whole group; a sorted map of counts makes this easy.

c-merge-triplets.title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
description: Merging two triplets takes the element-wise max. Return true if merging some of the triplets can produce exactly target.
c-merge-triplets.hint: Ignore triplets exceeding target anywhere; the rest can be merged freely, so check they reach every target value.

c-remove-covered-intervals.title: Remove Covered Intervals
description: Remove every interval covered by another ([a, b] is covered by [c, d] if c <= a and b <= d). Return how many intervals remain.
c-remove-covered-intervals.hint: Sort by start ascending, end descending; count intervals that extend past the maximum end so far.

c-min-deletions-unique-freq.title: Minimum Deletions to Make Character Frequencies Unique
description: Delete characters so that no two different characters have the same frequency. Return the minimum deletions.
c-min-deletions-unique-freq.hint: Sort frequencies descending; lower each one below the previous (stopping at 0), counting deletions.

c-broken-calculator.title: Broken Calculator
description: The calculator can only double the value or subtract 1. Return the fewest operations to turn startValue into target.
c-broken-calculator.hint: Work backwards from target: halve it when even, add 1 when odd, until it's <= startValue.

c-bag-of-tokens.title: Bag of Tokens
description: Play a token face up (pay its value in power, gain 1 score) or face down (gain its value in power, lose 1 score). Each token is used at most once. Return the maximum score.
c-bag-of-tokens.hint: Sort; buy score with the cheapest token, sell score for the most expensive one when stuck.

c-max-ice-cream.title: Maximum Ice Cream Bars
description: Return the most ice cream bars you can buy with coins.
c-max-ice-cream.hint: Buy the cheapest first (counting sort works for small costs).

c-min-cost-move-chips.title: Minimum Cost to Move Chips to The Same Position
description: Moving a chip by 2 is free; moving it by 1 costs 1. Return the minimum cost to move all chips to one position.
c-min-cost-move-chips.hint: Only parity matters: move the smaller parity group.

c-monotone-increasing-digits.title: Monotone Increasing Digits
description: Return the largest number <= n whose digits are non-decreasing from left to right.
c-monotone-increasing-digits.hint: Find the first drop, decrement that digit (moving left while it breaks order) and fill the rest with 9s.

c-wiggle-subsequence.title: Wiggle Subsequence
description: A wiggle sequence alternates strictly up and down. Return the length of the longest wiggle subsequence of nums.
c-wiggle-subsequence.hint: Count direction changes, ignoring equal neighbours.

c-reduce-array-half.title: Reduce Array Size to The Half
description: Choose a set of values and remove all their occurrences. Return the smallest set size that removes at least half of the array.
c-reduce-array-half.hint: Remove the most frequent values first.

c-preorder-traversal.title: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
description: Return the node values in preorder: node, then left subtree, then right subtree.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-preorder-traversal.hint: Recursion, or a stack: pop a node, record it, push right then left.

c-postorder-traversal.title: Binary Tree Postorder Traversal
description: Return the node values in postorder: left subtree, right subtree, then the node.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-postorder-traversal.hint: Recursion; iteratively, a reversed (node, right, left) preorder gives postorder.

c-symmetric-tree.title: Symmetric Tree
description: Return true if the tree is a mirror of itself around its centre.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-symmetric-tree.hint: mirror(a, b): both empty, or equal values with mirror(a.left, b.right) and mirror(a.right, b.left).

c-balanced-tree.title: Balanced Binary Tree
description: A tree is height-balanced if, at every node, the heights of the two subtrees differ by at most 1. Return whether the tree is balanced.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-balanced-tree.hint: Return -1 from the height function as soon as a subtree is unbalanced, so it's one O(n) pass.

c-min-depth.title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Return the number of nodes on the shortest path from the root down to a leaf (0 for an empty tree).
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-min-depth.hint: BFS and stop at the first leaf. In recursion, a node with one child isn't a leaf.

c-count-complete-nodes.title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
description: The tree is complete (every level full except possibly the last, filled from the left). Return its node count in less than O(n).
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-count-complete-nodes.hint: If the left-most and right-most depths match, the subtree is perfect: 2^h - 1 nodes. Otherwise recurse.

c-right-side-view.title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description: Return the values you'd see standing on the right of the tree: the last node of each level, top to bottom.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-right-side-view.hint: Level-order traversal keeping the last node of each level (or DFS visiting right first).

c-zigzag-level-order.title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
description: Return the level order traversal, alternating direction: left to right, then right to left, and so on.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-zigzag-level-order.hint: BFS by levels and reverse every other level.

c-top-view.title: Top View of Binary Tree
description: Give the root horizontal distance 0, a left child hd - 1 and a right child hd + 1. The top view is, for each hd from left to right, the first node reached in level order. Return those values.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-top-view.hint: BFS with (node, hd); record a node only for the first time its hd appears.

c-bottom-view.title: Bottom View of Binary Tree
description: With the same horizontal distances as Top View, the bottom view is, for each hd from left to right, the last node reached in level order. Return those values.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-bottom-view.hint: BFS with (node, hd); overwrite the map entry for an hd every time.

c-lca-bst.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
description: root is a binary search tree with distinct values. p and q are values of two nodes in it. Return the value of their lowest common ancestor (a node can be its own ancestor).
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-lca-bst.hint: If both values are smaller go left, both larger go right; otherwise you're at the split point.

c-lca-binary-tree.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
description: Values are distinct; p and q are values of two nodes in the tree. Return the value of their lowest common ancestor.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-lca-binary-tree.hint: Return the node if it's p or q; if both subtrees return something, this node is the LCA.

c-kth-smallest-bst.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
description: Return the k-th smallest value (1-based) in the binary search tree.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-kth-smallest-bst.hint: An inorder traversal visits a BST in sorted order; stop at the k-th node.

c-insert-into-bst.title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
description: Insert val (not already present) into the BST as a new leaf, following the usual rule (smaller goes left), and return the root.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-insert-into-bst.hint: Walk down comparing with each node until you reach an empty child spot.

c-search-bst.title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
description: Return the subtree rooted at the node whose value is val, or an empty tree if it isn't there.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-search-bst.hint: Go left when val is smaller, right when larger.

c-max-path-sum.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: A path is any sequence of connected nodes, each used once; it needn't pass through the root. Return the maximum path sum.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-max-path-sum.hint: At each node, the best downward gain is val + max(0, left gain, right gain); a path through it is val + both gains.

c-build-from-pre-in.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
description: Values are distinct. Rebuild the binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversals and return its root.
c-build-from-pre-in.hint: preorder[0] is the root; its position in inorder splits the left and right subtrees. Use a value -> index map.

c-sorted-array-to-bst.title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
description: nums is sorted ascending. Build a height-balanced BST by always choosing the left-middle element, nums[(lo + hi) / 2], as the root of each range. Return the root.
c-sorted-array-to-bst.hint: Recursively: the middle element becomes the root, the halves become the subtrees.

c-max-width-tree.title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
description: The width of a level is the distance between its leftmost and rightmost nodes, counting the null positions between them as in a complete tree. Return the maximum width.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-max-width-tree.hint: Number nodes like a heap (left 2i, right 2i + 1) during BFS; width = last - first + 1 per level.

c-count-good-nodes.title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
description: A node is good if no node on the path from the root to it has a greater value. Return how many good nodes there are.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-count-good-nodes.hint: DFS carrying the maximum seen on the path.

c-subtree-of-another.title: Subtree of Another Tree
description: Return true if some node of root has a subtree identical (structure and values) to subRoot.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-subtree-of-another.hint: For each node, check Same Tree against subRoot.

c-merge-two-trees.title: Merge Two Binary Trees
description: Overlay the two trees: overlapping nodes add their values; a node present in only one tree is used as is. Return the merged root.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-merge-two-trees.hint: Recursively: if either is empty return the other; otherwise add values and merge children.

c-binary-tree-paths.title: Binary Tree Paths
description: Return every root-to-leaf path as a string like "1->2->5", in DFS order (left subtree before right).
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-binary-tree-paths.hint: DFS carrying the path string; add it when you reach a leaf.

c-flatten-to-list.title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
description: Flatten the tree in place into a "linked list" using right pointers, in preorder, with every left child null. Return the root.
The tree is given in level order with null for missing children; your function receives the root TreeNode (val, left, right).
c-flatten-to-list.hint: For each node, hang the right subtree under the right-most node of the left subtree, then move left to right.

c-kth-largest-stream.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
description: Start with nums. After each value in adds is added to the stream, record the k-th largest value so far. Return those records. (There are always at least k values after each add.)
c-kth-largest-stream.hint: Keep a min-heap of size k; its top is the k-th largest.

c-kth-smallest-element.title: Kth Smallest Element
description: Return the k-th smallest value of nums (1-based), using a heap rather than a full sort.
c-kth-smallest-element.hint: A max-heap of size k holds the k smallest; its top is the answer.

c-merge-k-sorted-arrays.title: Merge K Sorted Arrays
description: Each row is sorted ascending. Return one sorted array with every element.
c-merge-k-sorted-arrays.hint: Push the first element of each row as (value, row, index); pop the smallest and push its row's next element.

c-sort-k-sorted.title: Sort a Nearly Sorted Array
description: Every element is at most k positions away from its sorted position. Sort nums in O(n log k).
c-sort-k-sorted.hint: Keep a min-heap of the next k + 1 elements; pop the minimum each step.

c-connect-ropes.title: Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes
description: Connecting two ropes of lengths a and b costs a + b and gives a rope of length a + b. Return the minimum total cost to connect all ropes into one.
c-connect-ropes.hint: Always connect the two shortest ropes (Huffman style).

c-running-median.title: Find Median from Data Stream
description: Values (all non-negative) arrive one by one. After each arrival, record the median of the values so far, rounded down when it's the average of two middle values. Return the records.
c-running-median.hint: Two heaps: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, balanced in size.

c-top-k-frequent-words.title: Top K Frequent Words
description: Return the k most frequent words, most frequent first. Words with the same frequency go in lexicographic order.
c-top-k-frequent-words.hint: Count, then select with a heap ordered by (count desc, word asc).

c-kth-smallest-sorted-matrix.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
description: Each row and column of the n x n matrix is sorted ascending. Return the k-th smallest element.
c-kth-smallest-sorted-matrix.hint: Min-heap seeded with the first column, popping k times; or binary search on the value.

c-k-smallest-pairs.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
description: nums1 and nums2 are sorted. Return the k pairs [u, v] (u from nums1, v from nums2) with the smallest sums, ordered by sum, then by u, then by v.
c-k-smallest-pairs.hint: Heap of (sum, i, j) seeded with (i, 0) for each i; when popping (i, j), push (i, j + 1).

c-furthest-building.title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
description: Moving from building i to i + 1 is free if it's not taller; otherwise climb with bricks (one per unit of height difference) or one ladder. Return the furthest building index you can reach.
c-furthest-building.hint: Use ladders on the largest climbs: keep a min-heap of climbs and pay bricks for the smallest when it overflows ladders.

c-max-performance-team.title: Maximum Performance of a Team
description: Pick at most k of the n engineers. A team's performance is (sum of speeds) x (minimum efficiency). Return the maximum performance modulo 1,000,000,007.
c-max-performance-team.hint: Sort by efficiency descending; keep a min-heap of the k largest speeds so far.

c-ipo.title: IPO
description: You start with capital w and may finish at most k projects. Project i needs capital[i] to start and adds profits[i] to your capital. Return the maximum final capital.
c-ipo.hint: Sort projects by capital; unlock affordable ones into a max-heap of profits and take the best each round.

c-single-threaded-cpu.title: Single-Threaded CPU
description: tasks[i] = [enqueueTime, processingTime]. When idle, the CPU picks the available task with the shortest processing time (smallest index on ties) and runs it to completion. Return the order of task indices.
c-single-threaded-cpu.hint: Sort by enqueue time; a heap of (processing, index) holds the available tasks; jump the clock when idle.

c-smallest-range-k-lists.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
description: Each list is sorted. Return the smallest range [a, b] that includes at least one number from every list. Smaller b - a wins; on a tie, the smaller a wins.
c-smallest-range-k-lists.hint: Heap of the current element of each list; track the max; advance the list holding the min.

c-remove-stones-min-total.title: Remove Stones to Minimize the Total
description: k times, choose a pile and remove floor(pile / 2) stones from it (the same pile may be chosen again). Return the minimum total stones left.
c-remove-stones-min-total.hint: Always halve the largest pile: max-heap.

c-gifts-from-richest.title: Take Gifts From the Richest Pile
description: Each second for k seconds, take the largest pile and leave floor(sqrt(pile)) gifts in it. Return the gifts left in total.

c-min-cost-hire-workers.title: Minimum Cost to Hire K Workers
description: Hire exactly k workers. Each is paid in proportion to quality relative to the others in the group, and at least their minimum wage. Return the least total pay.
c-min-cost-hire-workers.hint: Sort by wage/quality ratio; for each ratio as the group's rate, keep the k smallest qualities in a max-heap.

c-ugly-number-ii.title: Ugly Number II
description: Ugly numbers have only 2, 3 and 5 as prime factors (1 is the first). Return the n-th ugly number.
c-ugly-number-ii.hint: Min-heap with a seen set, or three pointers multiplying by 2, 3 and 5.

c-super-ugly-number.title: Super Ugly Number
description: A super ugly number has all prime factors in primes (1 is the first). Return the n-th one.
c-super-ugly-number.hint: One pointer per prime into the result list, like Ugly Number II.

c-max-score-k-ops.title: Maximal Score After Applying K Operations
description: k times: pick any index, add nums[i] to your score and replace nums[i] with ceil(nums[i] / 3). Return the maximum score.

c-k-max-sum-combinations.title: K Maximum Sum Combinations
description: Return the k largest sums a[i] + b[j] (each pair of indices counts once), largest first.
c-k-max-sum-combinations.hint: Sort both descending; a max-heap of (sum, i, j) with a visited set expands (i + 1, j) and (i, j + 1).

c-relative-ranks.title: Relative Ranks
description: Scores are distinct. The top three get "Gold Medal", "Silver Medal" and "Bronze Medal"; everyone else gets their placement number as a string. Return each athlete's rank in input order.
c-relative-ranks.hint: Sort indices by score descending (or use a max-heap) and assign labels.

c-max-product-k-increments.title: Maximum Product After K Increments
description: k times, increment any element by 1. Return the maximum product of all elements, modulo 1,000,000,007.
c-max-product-k-increments.hint: Always increment the smallest element: min-heap.

c-halve-array-sum.title: Minimum Operations to Halve Array Sum
description: An operation halves any one number (it can become a fraction). Return the minimum operations to reduce the array's sum by at least half.
c-halve-array-sum.hint: Halve the current largest value each time (max-heap of doubles).

c-total-cost-hire-k.title: Total Cost to Hire K Workers
description: Hire k workers in k rounds. Each round, pick the cheapest worker among the first `candidates` and last `candidates` remaining workers (smallest index on ties); they leave the line. Return the total cost.
c-total-cost-hire-k.hint: Two min-heaps for the left and right candidate windows, refilled from the middle.

c-course-schedule-iii.title: Course Schedule III
description: courses[i] = [duration, lastDay]. Courses are taken one at a time starting on day 1 and must finish by lastDay. Return the maximum number of courses you can take.
c-course-schedule-iii.hint: Sort by deadline; add each course, and if time overflows drop the longest course taken (max-heap).

c-subsets-ii.title: Subsets II
description: nums may contain duplicates. Return all distinct subsets; each subset sorted ascending, the list in lexicographic order.
c-subsets-ii.hint: Sort first; at each level skip a value equal to the previous one at the same depth.

c-combination-sum.title: Combination Sum
description: candidates are distinct positive integers, each usable any number of times. Return every unique combination summing to target, each sorted ascending, the list in lexicographic order.
c-combination-sum.hint: Recurse with a start index; you may stay on the same candidate to reuse it.

c-combination-sum-ii.title: Combination Sum II
description: Each candidate may be used once and candidates may repeat. Return every unique combination summing to target, each sorted ascending, the list in lexicographic order.
c-combination-sum-ii.hint: Sort; skip equal values at the same depth; move to i + 1 after choosing i.

c-combination-sum-iii.title: Combination Sum III
description: Find all combinations of k distinct numbers from 1-9 that sum to n. Each combination ascending, the list in lexicographic order.
c-combination-sum-iii.hint: Choose numbers in increasing order and prune when the sum overshoots.

c-combinations.title: Combinations
description: Return all combinations of k numbers chosen from 1..n, each ascending, in lexicographic order.
c-combinations.hint: Recurse choosing the next number after the last chosen one.

c-permutations-ii.title: Permutations II
description: nums may contain duplicates. Return all distinct permutations in lexicographic order.
c-permutations-ii.hint: Sort, and skip nums[i] if it equals nums[i - 1] and nums[i - 1] isn't used in the current path.

c-letter-combinations-phone.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
description: Digits 2-9 map to letters as on a phone keypad (2 = abc, ..., 7 = pqrs, 9 = wxyz). Return every letter combination the digits could spell, in lexicographic order. Empty input gives an empty list.
c-letter-combinations-phone.hint: One recursion level per digit, looping over its letters.

c-palindrome-partitioning.title: Palindrome Partitioning
description: Return every way to split s into palindromic parts. Write each partition as its parts joined by '|' (e.g. "a|a|b"), in the order a depth-first search tries shorter first parts first.
c-palindrome-partitioning.hint: At each start index, try every end index whose substring is a palindrome, recurse on the rest.

c-word-search.title: Word Search
description: board is a grid of letters (one string per row). Return true if word can be traced through adjacent cells (up, down, left, right), using each cell at most once.
c-word-search.hint: DFS from every cell, marking cells as visited on the way in and unmarking on the way out.

c-n-queens-ii.title: N-Queens II
description: Return how many ways n queens can be placed on an n x n board so that no two attack each other.
c-n-queens-ii.hint: Place one queen per row; track used columns and both diagonals (r + c and r - c).

c-sudoku-solver.title: Sudoku Solver
description: board is 9 strings of 9 characters, digits or '.' for empty. The puzzle has exactly one solution. Return the solved board in the same format.
c-sudoku-solver.hint: Find an empty cell, try digits that don't clash with its row, column and box, recurse, undo on failure.

c-rat-in-maze.title: Rat in a Maze
description: The rat starts at the top-left of an n x n maze (1 = open, 0 = blocked) and must reach the bottom-right, moving U, D, L or R without revisiting a cell. Return every path as a string of moves, in lexicographic order.
c-rat-in-maze.hint: DFS trying D, L, R, U (alphabetical) with a visited grid; record the path at the target.

c-m-coloring.title: M-Coloring Problem
description: Return true if the undirected graph with vertices 0..n-1 can be coloured with at most m colours so that no edge joins two vertices of the same colour.
c-m-coloring.hint: Assign colours vertex by vertex, checking only already-coloured neighbours; backtrack on conflict.

c-word-break-ii.title: Word Break II
description: Insert spaces into s so every word is in wordDict (words may be reused). Return every possible sentence, sorted lexicographically.
c-word-break-ii.hint: Recurse on each dictionary prefix; memoise results by start index.

c-restore-ip-addresses.title: Restore IP Addresses
description: Insert three dots into the digit string s to form valid IPv4 addresses (four parts 0-255, no leading zeros except "0" itself). Return all of them, sorted lexicographically.
c-restore-ip-addresses.hint: Choose 1-3 digits for each of the four parts, validating as you go.

c-letter-case-permutation.title: Letter Case Permutation
description: Each letter of s may be lowercase or uppercase. Return every resulting string, sorted lexicographically.
c-letter-case-permutation.hint: Branch on each letter (lower and upper), pass digits through.

c-beautiful-arrangement.title: Beautiful Arrangement
description: A permutation perm of 1..n is beautiful if for every position i (1-based), perm[i] is divisible by i or i is divisible by perm[i]. Return how many beautiful permutations exist.
c-beautiful-arrangement.hint: Fill positions one by one with unused numbers that satisfy the rule.

c-expression-add-operators.title: Expression Add Operators
description: Insert +, - or * between the digits of num (operands may not have leading zeros) so the expression evaluates to target. Return all such expressions, sorted lexicographically.
c-expression-add-operators.hint: Recurse carrying the running value and the last operand, so * can undo and redo the last term.

c-partition-k-equal-subsets.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
description: Return true if nums can be divided into k non-empty subsets with equal sums.
c-partition-k-equal-subsets.hint: Sort descending; fill buckets with backtracking, skipping buckets with the same current sum.

c-matchsticks-square.title: Matchsticks to Square
description: Return true if all matchsticks can form a square (each used exactly once, none broken).

c-split-descending-consecutive.title: Splitting a String Into Descending Consecutive Values
description: Return true if s can be split into two or more substrings whose numeric values are in descending order with each adjacent pair differing by exactly 1.
c-split-descending-consecutive.hint: Try every first number, then greedily look for value - 1 next.

c-max-length-unique-concat.title: Maximum Length of a Concatenated String with Unique Characters
description: Choose a subsequence of arr whose concatenation has all distinct characters. Return the maximum possible length.
c-max-length-unique-concat.hint: Include or skip each word, keeping a 26-bit mask of used letters.

c-additive-number.title: Additive Number
description: An additive number's digits split into at least three numbers where each is the sum of the two before it (no leading zeros). Return whether num is additive.
c-additive-number.hint: Choose the first two numbers; the rest is forced. Use big integers or long.

c-path-max-gold.title: Path with Maximum Gold
description: Each cell has some gold (0 = empty, can't enter). Start anywhere with gold, move up/down/left/right, never revisit a cell, and collect gold as you go. Return the most gold you can collect.
c-path-max-gold.hint: DFS from every gold cell, temporarily zeroing cells on the path.

c-unique-paths-iii.title: Unique Paths III
description: In the grid, 1 is the start, 2 the end, 0 empty and -1 an obstacle. Count the 4-directional walks from start to end that visit every non-obstacle cell exactly once.
c-unique-paths-iii.hint: DFS counting remaining empty cells; a walk counts only if it reaches 2 with none left.

c-word-search-ii.title: Word Search II
description: Return every word from words that can be traced on the board (adjacent cells, each used once per word), sorted lexicographically.
c-word-search-ii.hint: Put the words in a trie and DFS the board once, walking the trie as you go.

c-letter-tile-possibilities.title: Letter Tile Possibilities
description: Return how many distinct non-empty sequences of letters you can make using the tiles (each tile at most once per sequence).
c-letter-tile-possibilities.hint: Backtrack over letter counts: for each letter with count > 0, use it, count 1, recurse, restore.

c-fair-cookies.title: Fair Distribution of Cookies
description: Give every bag of cookies to one of k children. The unfairness is the largest total any child gets. Return the minimum unfairness.
c-fair-cookies.hint: Assign bags one by one to each child, pruning when a child's total already exceeds the best answer.

c-bfs-traversal.title: BFS of a Graph
description: Return the breadth-first order of vertices reachable from 0, visiting each vertex's neighbours in increasing order.
Vertices are 0..n-1; edges lists undirected edges [u, v].
c-bfs-traversal.hint: Queue plus a visited array; mark a vertex when you enqueue it.

c-dfs-traversal.title: DFS of a Graph
description: Return the recursive depth-first order of vertices reachable from 0, visiting neighbours in increasing order.
Vertices are 0..n-1; edges lists undirected edges [u, v].
c-dfs-traversal.hint: Recurse into each unvisited neighbour before moving to the next one.

c-connected-components.title: Number of Connected Components
description: Return the number of connected components.
Vertices are 0..n-1; edges lists undirected edges [u, v].
c-connected-components.hint: DFS/BFS from each unvisited vertex, or union-find.

c-cycle-undirected.title: Detect Cycle in an Undirected Graph
description: Return true if the undirected graph contains a cycle.
Vertices are 0..n-1; edges lists undirected edges [u, v].
c-cycle-undirected.hint: DFS remembering the parent: reaching a visited vertex that isn't the parent means a cycle. Or union-find.

c-cycle-directed.title: Detect Cycle in a Directed Graph
description: Vertices are 0..n-1; edges lists directed edges [u, v] meaning u -> v. Return true if the graph has a cycle.
c-cycle-directed.hint: DFS with a recursion-stack flag, or Kahn's algorithm (a cycle leaves vertices unprocessed).

c-topological-sort.title: Topological Sort
description: edges are directed [u, v] (u must come before v) and the graph is acyclic. Return the topological order that, at each step, takes the smallest available vertex.
c-topological-sort.hint: Kahn's algorithm with a min-heap instead of a queue.

c-course-schedule-ii.title: Course Schedule II
description: prerequisites[i] = [a, b] means take b before a. Return an order to take all courses, choosing the smallest available course at each step, or an empty array if impossible.
c-course-schedule-ii.hint: Kahn's algorithm (smallest first); if fewer than numCourses are output, there's a cycle.

c-is-bipartite.title: Is Graph Bipartite?
description: graph[u] lists the neighbours of u (undirected). Return true if the vertices can be split into two groups with every edge going between the groups.
c-is-bipartite.hint: BFS/DFS colouring each component with two colours; a clash means not bipartite.

c-surrounded-regions.title: Surrounded Regions
description: board has 'X' and 'O'. Capture every region of 'O' that is not connected to the border by flipping it to 'X'. Return the board.
c-surrounded-regions.hint: Mark every 'O' reachable from the border; flip all other 'O's.

c-number-of-enclaves.title: Number of Enclaves
description: grid has 1 (land) and 0 (sea). Return how many land cells can't walk off the grid's edge.
c-number-of-enclaves.hint: Flood fill from all border land cells, then count land left.

c-01-matrix.title: 01 Matrix
description: mat is binary with at least one 0. Return the distance from each cell to its nearest 0 (moving up/down/left/right).

c-word-ladder.title: Word Ladder
description: Change one letter at a time; every intermediate word must be in wordList. Return the number of words in the shortest sequence from beginWord to endWord, or 0 if impossible.
c-word-ladder.hint: BFS over words, trying every letter at every position.

c-shortest-path-unweighted.title: Shortest Path in an Undirected Graph
description: Every edge has length 1. Return the shortest distance from src to every vertex, or -1 if unreachable.
Vertices are 0..n-1; edges lists undirected edges [u, v].
c-shortest-path-unweighted.hint: Plain BFS gives shortest paths when all edges weigh 1.

c-dijkstra.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Paths
description: edges are undirected [u, v, w] with non-negative weights. Return the shortest distance from src to every vertex, or -1 if unreachable.
c-dijkstra.hint: Min-heap of (distance, vertex); skip stale entries.

c-network-delay-time.title: Network Delay Time
description: Nodes are 1..n; times[i] = [u, v, w] is a directed edge taking w time. A signal starts at k. Return the time for all nodes to receive it, or -1 if some never do.
c-network-delay-time.hint: Dijkstra from k; the answer is the largest distance.

c-cheapest-flights-k-stops.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
description: flights[i] = [from, to, price] (directed). Return the cheapest price from src to dst with at most k stops, or -1.
c-cheapest-flights-k-stops.hint: Bellman-Ford limited to k + 1 rounds, copying the distance array each round.

c-path-minimum-effort.title: Path With Minimum Effort
description: Walk from the top-left to the bottom-right (up/down/left/right). A path's effort is its largest absolute height difference between consecutive cells. Return the minimum effort.
c-path-minimum-effort.hint: Dijkstra where a path's cost is the max edge on it.

c-shortest-path-binary-matrix.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
description: Return the number of cells on the shortest path of 0s from the top-left to the bottom-right, moving in 8 directions, or -1 if there is none.
c-shortest-path-binary-matrix.hint: BFS with 8 neighbours; the start and end must be 0.

c-bellman-ford.title: Bellman-Ford
description: edges are directed [u, v, w]; weights may be negative. Return shortest distances from src (use 100000000 for unreachable). If a negative cycle is reachable from src, return [-1].
c-bellman-ford.hint: Relax every edge n - 1 times; one more successful relaxation means a negative cycle.

c-floyd-warshall.title: Floyd-Warshall
description: matrix[i][j] is the weight of the directed edge i -> j, or -1 if there is no edge (matrix[i][i] = 0). Return the matrix of shortest distances, keeping -1 where j is unreachable from i.
c-floyd-warshall.hint: For every k, i, j: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]).
